tasks.prompt: Trace hum back to its origin, step by step.
tasks.answer: Huwū (the plain plural of huwa); the wāw was made a mīm because wāw and mīm share their point of articulation and two wāws met: humū; then the final wāw dropped, as in ḍarabtumū: hum.

tasks.prompt: Why does huwa keep its wāw alone, but lose it in lahu?
tasks.answer: Alone, huwa has fewer letters than the proper measure, so the wāw cannot go. Embraced by the lām, the two words together have letters enough, and the wāw stands at the end, so it drops, while the hāʾ keeps its ḍamma.

tasks.prompt: Why ghulāmihi and fīhi, but lahu?
tasks.answer: After a kasra (ghulāmi-) or a quiescent yāʾ (fī-) the hāʾ takes a kasra, so as not to go from a kasra to a ḍamma; after a fatḥa (la-) it keeps its ḍamma.

quiz.prompt: The plain plural of huwa would have been…
quiz.explanation: Then the wāw became a mīm: humū, hum.

quiz.prompt: Why was the wāw made a mīm in hum?
options: They share a point of articulation, and two wāws met
The mīm is a throat letter
quiz.explanation: Wāw and mīm are both letters of the lips.

quiz.prompt: The wāw of huwa is not dropped when it stands alone because…
options: the word would be below the proper measure
quiz.explanation: Two letters are too few to lose one.

quiz.prompt: In lahu, the wāw of huwa…
quiz.explanation: The joined letters are enough, and the wāw stands at the end.

quiz.prompt: The hāʾ of fīhi has a kasra because…
options: a quiescent yāʾ stands before it
quiz.explanation: So as not to go from kasra to ḍamma.

quiz.prompt: In the dual of hiya, the yāʾ becomes…
quiz.explanation: Humā: the fatḥa should not fall on the weak yāʾ.

quiz.prompt: Yā ghulāmā for yā ghulāmī shows…
quiz.explanation: As the yāʾ of hiya may be made an alif.

text.original: الْأَصْلُ فِي هُوَ أَنْ يُقَالَ: هُوَا، هُوُوا، وَلَكِنْ جُعِلَ الْوَاوُ مِيمًا فِي الْجَمْعِ لِاتِّحَادِ مَخْرَجِهِمَا وَاجْتِمَاعِ الْوَاوَيْنِ، فَصَارَ هُمُوا، ثُمَّ حُذِفَتِ الْوَاوُ كَمَا فِي ضَرَبْتُمُوا، وَحُمِلَتِ التَّثْنِيَةُ عَلَيْهِ، وَقِيلَ: حَتَّى تَقَعَ الْفَتْحَةُ عَلَى الْمِيمِ الْقَوِيِّ. وَأُدْخِلَ الْمِيمُ فِي أَنْتُمَا كَمَا مَرَّ فِي ضَرَبْتُمَا، وَحُمِلَ الْجَمْعُ عَلَيْهِ.
text.en: The origin of huwa [in the dual and the plural] is that one says huwā and huwū; but the wāw was made a mīm in the plural, because their point of articulation is one and two wāws come together, so it became humū; then the wāw was dropped, as in ḍarabtumū, and the dual was treated like it; and it is said: so that the fatḥa falls on the strong mīm. The mīm was put into antumā “you two”, as has passed in ḍarabtumā, and the plural was treated like it.

text.original: وَلَا يُحْذَفُ وَاوُ هُوَ لِقِلَّةِ حُرُوفِهِ مِنَ الْقَدْرِ الصَّالِحِ، وَيُحْذَفُ إِذَا تَعَانَقَ بِشَيْءٍ آخَرَ؛ لِحُصُولِ كَثْرَةِ الْحُرُوفِ بِالْمُعَانَقَةِ، مَعَ وُقُوعِ الْوَاوِ فِي الطَّرَفِ، وَيَبْقَى الْهَاءُ مَضْمُومًا عَلَى حَالِهِ، نَحْوُ: لَهُ، وَيُكْسَرُ الْهَاءُ إِذَا كَانَ مَا قَبْلَهُ مَكْسُورًا أَوْ يَاءً سَاكِنَةً حَتَّى لَا يَلْزَمَ الْخُرُوجُ مِنَ الْكَسْرَةِ إِلَى الضَّمَّةِ، نَحْوُ: غُلَامِهِ وَفِيهِ.
text.en: The wāw of huwa is not dropped, because its letters are fewer than the proper measure; it is dropped when it is embraced by something else, because many letters are obtained by the embracing, together with the wāw's falling at the end; and the hāʾ remains with its ḍamma as it was, as lahu “to him”. The hāʾ takes a kasra when what is before it has a kasra or is an unvowelled yāʾ, so that going from a kasra to a ḍamma is not required, as ghulāmihi “his servant (gen.)” and fīhi “in it”.

text.original: وَيُجْعَلُ يَاءُ هِيَ أَلِفًا كَمَا يُجْعَلُ فِي يَا غُلَامِي: يَا غُلَامَا، وَفِي يَا بَادِيَةُ: يَا بَادَاةُ، وَيُجْعَلُ الْيَاءُ مِيمًا فِي التَّثْنِيَةِ حَتَّى لَا تَقَعَ الْفَتْحَةُ عَلَى الْيَاءِ الضَّعِيفِ مَعَ ضَعْفِهَا، وَشُدِّدَ نُونُ هُنَّ كَمَا مَرَّ فِي ضَرَبْتُنَّ.
text.en: The yāʾ of hiya “she” is made an alif, as it is made in yā ghulāmī “O my servant”: yā ghulāmā, and in yā bādiyatu “O desert”: yā bādātu; and the yāʾ is made a mīm in the dual, so that the fatḥa does not fall on the weak yāʾ, weak as it is. The nūn of hunna “they (f.)” was doubled, as has passed in ḍarabtunna.

lessons.title: The object pronouns and the pronouns in jarr
body: Twelve attached manṣūb pronouns follow the verb as its object: ḍarabahu, “he hit him”, to ḍarabanā, “he hit us”. One combination is not allowed: the pronoun of the doer and the pronoun of the object for the same person, as ḍarabtaka, “you hit you”, or ḍarabtunī, “I hit me”, “so that one person does not become doer and object in one state”. To hit oneself, Arabic uses a noun: ḍarabta nafsaka, “you hit yourself”.

The exception is “the verbs of the heart” (afʿāl al-qulūb), verbs of knowing and thinking with two objects: ʿalimtaka fāḍilan, “you knew yourself to be excellent”, ʿalimtunī fāḍilan, “I knew myself to be excellent”. These are allowed “because the first object is not an object in reality”: what is known is not the person but a fact about him, and the sentence means ʿalimta faḍlaka, “you knew your excellence”.

Twelve separate manṣūb pronouns are built on iyyā-: iyyāhu ḍaraba, “him he hit”, to iyyānā ḍaraba, “us he hit”. They are used when the object comes first, or cannot be attached. Twelve attached majrūr pronouns are joined to a noun in iḍāfa or to a preposition: ḍāribuhu, “the one hitting him”, to ḍāribunā, “the one hitting us”.

One form needs explaining: ḍāribiyya, “those hitting me”. The plural ḍāribūna loses its nūn in iḍāfa and meets the yāʾ of “me”: ḍāribūya. Then “the wāw was made a yāʾ and assimilated, as in mahdiyy”, the passive participle whose origin is mahdūy (lesson 57). A wāw and a yāʾ side by side, the first quiescent, become a doubled yāʾ: a rule the hollow and defective chapters use again and again.

terms.en: the object pronoun: -hu, -ka, -nī … and iyyā-
the pronoun in jarr, joined to a noun or a preposition
the verbs of the heart: knowing and thinking, with two objects
the base of the separate object pronouns

examples.en: ḍarabahu to ḍarabanā: the twelve attached manṣūb
ʿalimtaka fāḍilan, ʿalimtunī fāḍilan: doer and object one person, with a verb of the heart
ʿalimta faḍlaka: what the sentence means
ḍāribiyya: from ḍāribūya, the wāw made yāʾ and assimilated

tasks.prompt: Why is ḍarabtunī not said, while ʿalimtunī fāḍilan is?
tasks.answer: In ḍarabtunī one person would be doer and object of the same act at once, which is not allowed. ʿAlimtunī fāḍilan has a verb of the heart, whose first object is not really an object: the sentence means ʿalimtu faḍlī, “I knew my excellence”.

tasks.prompt: Name the class of each pronoun: the -hu of ḍarabahu, the -hu of ḍāribuhu, iyyāhu.
tasks.answer: Ḍarabahu: attached manṣūb (object of the verb). Ḍāribuhu: attached majrūr (in iḍāfa). Iyyāhu: separate manṣūb.

tasks.prompt: Explain ḍāribiyya.
tasks.answer: Ḍāribūna, annexed to the yāʾ of “me”, loses its nūn: ḍāribūya. The quiescent wāw before the yāʾ is made a yāʾ and assimilated into it, as in mahdiyy from mahdūy: ḍāribiyya.

quiz.prompt: Ḍarabahu to ḍarabanā are the twelve…
quiz.explanation: Object pronouns joined to the verb.

quiz.prompt: Why is ḍarabtaka not allowed?
options: One person would be doer and object at once
The kāf is a throat letter
quiz.explanation: Except with the verbs of the heart.

quiz.prompt: Which verb allows ʿalimtunī fāḍilan?
quiz.explanation: Its first object is not an object in reality.

quiz.prompt: ʿAlimtaka fāḍilan is taken to mean…
quiz.explanation: “You knew your excellence.”

quiz.prompt: Iyyāhu ḍaraba is an example of the…
quiz.explanation: The object pronoun standing on its own, before the verb.

quiz.prompt: Ḍāribuhu shows the pronoun…
quiz.explanation: The pronoun is in jarr by iḍāfa.

quiz.prompt: Ḍāribiyya is compared with…
quiz.explanation: In both a wāw before a yāʾ became a yāʾ and was assimilated.

text.original: وَاثْنَا عَشَرَ لِلْمَنْصُوبِ الْمُتَّصِلِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَهُ إِلَى ضَرَبَنَا، وَلَا يَجُوزُ فِيهِ اجْتِمَاعُ ضَمِيرَيِ الْفَاعِلِ وَالْمَفْعُولِ فِي مِثْلِ: ضَرَبْتَكَ وَضَرَبْتُنِي، حَتَّى لَا يَصِيرَ الشَّخْصُ الْوَاحِدُ فَاعِلًا وَمَفْعُولًا فِي حَالَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، إِلَّا فِي أَفْعَالِ الْقُلُوبِ، نَحْوُ: عَلِمْتَكَ فَاضِلًا، وَعَلِمْتُنِي فَاضِلًا؛ لِأَنَّ الْمَفْعُولَ الْأَوَّلَ لَيْسَ بِمَفْعُولٍ فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ، وَلِهَذَا قِيلَ فِي تَقْدِيرِهِ: عَلِمْتَ فَضْلَكَ، وَعَلِمْتُ فَضْلِي.
text.en: Twelve are for the attached manṣūb, as ḍarabahu “he hit him” to ḍarabanā “he hit us”. In it the coming together of the pronouns of the fāʿil and the mafʿūl is not allowed, in the like of ḍarabtaka and ḍarabtunī, so that one person does not become fāʿil and mafʿūl in one state — except in the verbs of the heart, as ʿalimtaka fāḍilan “you knew yourself to be excellent” and ʿalimtunī fāḍilan “I knew myself to be excellent”, because the first object is not an object in reality; for this reason it is said in its implied [wording]: ʿalimta faḍlaka “you knew your excellence” and ʿalimtu faḍlī “I knew my excellence”.

text.original: وَاثْنَا عَشَرَ لِلْمَنْصُوبِ الْمُنْفَصِلِ، نَحْوُ: إِيَّاهُ ضَرَبَ إِلَى إِيَّانَا ضَرَبَ، وَاثْنَا عَشَرَ لِلْمَجْرُورِ الْمُتَّصِلِ، نَحْوُ: ضَارِبُهُ إِلَى ضَارِبُنَا، وَفِي مِثْلِ: ضَارِبِيَّ جُعِلَ الْوَاوُ يَاءً ثُمَّ أُدْغِمَ، كَمَا فِي مَهْدِيٍّ.
text.en: Twelve are for the separate manṣūb, as iyyāhu ḍaraba “him he hit” to iyyānā ḍaraba “us he hit”; and twelve for the attached majrūr, as ḍāribuhu “the one hitting him” to ḍāribunā “the one hitting us”. In the like of ḍāribiyya “those hitting me” the wāw was made a yāʾ and then assimilated, as in mahdiyyin “guided”.

lessons.title: The hidden pronoun, and the yāʾ of taḍribīna
body: Not every pronoun is seen. “The attached marfūʿ is hidden in five places”, present in the meaning but with no letter of its own. Three are given here: the absent man (ḍaraba, yaḍribu, li-yaḍrib, lā yaḍrib: “he” hit, hits, let him hit, let him not), the absent woman (ḍarabat, taḍribu, li-taḍrib, lā taḍrib), and the man addressed “outside the past” (taḍribu, iḍrib, lā taḍrib). The speaker and the adjective follow in the next lesson.

Note the third place: “outside the past”. In the past the man addressed has a visible pronoun, the -ta of ḍarabta; in the future and the command he has none, and taḍribu or iḍrib carry the “you” within them.

Then a question that divided the grammarians: what is the yāʾ of taḍribīna, “you (a woman) hit”? For al-Akhfash it is only “a sign of address”, and the doer is hidden; for most, it is “a visible pronoun of the doer, like the wāw of yaḍribūna”. Either way, why a yāʾ? Because the yāʾ is at home with the feminine: in hādhī amatu Allāhi, “this is the handmaid of God”, hādhī ends in yāʾ.

Why not a letter of anti, as ḍarabtu took a letter near anā? An alif would look like the dual taḍribāni; a nūn would put two nūns together; a tāʾ would repeat the tāʾ of the prefix. Why must the yāʾ show? To tell her from the women's plural, taḍribna. Why not a vowel alone, taḍribinna? It would look like the heavy nūn of emphasis. And why keep the nūn? Without it, the form would be confused with the man addressed.

This is the Marāḥ's method at its fullest: every alternative the language could have used is named and ruled out with a reason. Read such a passage as a list of options and objections, not as a story.

terms.en: the hidden pronoun: meant but not written
the visible pronoun: written and heard
a sign of address, not a pronoun: al-Akhfash on the yāʾ of taḍribīna
a Baṣran grammarian whose views the book reports

examples.en: ḍaraba, yaḍribu, wa-lyaḍrib, wa-lā yaḍrib: the hidden “he”
taḍribu, iḍrib, lā taḍrib: the hidden “you” outside the past
hādhī amatu Allāhi: the yāʾ at home with the feminine

tasks.prompt: In which of these is the doer's pronoun hidden, and in which visible: ḍarabta, taḍribu (“you hit”), iḍrib, ḍarabū?
tasks.answer: Visible in ḍarabta (-ta) and ḍarabū (-ū); hidden in taḍribu and iḍrib, for the man addressed outside the past has a hidden pronoun.

tasks.prompt: Give both views of the yāʾ of taḍribīna.
tasks.answer: Al-Akhfash: it is only a sign of address, and the doer is hidden. Most grammarians: it is a visible pronoun of the doer, like the wāw of yaḍribūna.

tasks.prompt: Why was none of the letters of anti added to taḍribīna?
tasks.answer: The alif would make it look like the dual taḍribāni; the nūn would bring two nūns together; the tāʾ would repeat the tāʾ already at the start of the word.

quiz.prompt: In how many places is the attached marfūʿ hidden?
quiz.explanation: Absent man, absent woman, man addressed outside the past, speaker, adjective.

quiz.prompt: Where is the pronoun of the man addressed visible?
quiz.explanation: Ḍarabta has -ta; taḍribu and iḍrib have none.

quiz.prompt: For al-Akhfash, the yāʾ of taḍribīna is…
options: the visible pronoun of the doer
a sign of address, with the doer hidden
quiz.explanation: Most others call it a visible pronoun.

quiz.prompt: Why was the yāʾ chosen for taḍribīna?
options: It comes for the feminine, as in hādhī
It is a letter of anti
quiz.explanation: Hādhī amatu Allāhi.

quiz.prompt: Why not an alif in taḍribīna?
options: It would look like the plural
It would look like the dual
It would look like the past
quiz.explanation: Taḍribāni is the dual.

quiz.prompt: Why must the yāʾ of taḍribīna be visible?
options: To tell it from the past
To tell it from the women's plural taḍribna
quiz.explanation: “The yāʾ was made visible to distinguish it from its plural.”

quiz.prompt: Which form has a hidden “he”?
quiz.explanation: The absent man's pronoun is hidden.

text.original: وَالْمَرْفُوعُ الْمُتَّصِلُ يَسْتَتِرُ فِي خَمْسَةِ مَوَاضِعَ: فِي الْغَائِبِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَ وَيَضْرِبُ وَلْيَضْرِبْ وَلَا يَضْرِبْ، وَفِي الْغَائِبَةِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَتْ وَتَضْرِبُ وَلْتَضْرِبْ وَلَا تَضْرِبْ، وَفِي الْمُخَاطَبِ الَّذِي فِي غَيْرِ الْمَاضِي، نَحْوُ: تَضْرِبُ وَاضْرِبْ وَلَا تَضْرِبْ.
text.en: The attached marfūʿ is hidden in five places: in the absent man, as ḍaraba “he hit”, yaḍribu “he hits”, wa-lyaḍrib “and let him hit” and wa-lā yaḍrib “and let him not hit”; in the absent woman, as ḍarabat “she hit”, wa-taḍribu “and she hits”, wa-ltaḍrib “and let her hit” and wa-lā taḍrib “and let her not hit”; and in the man addressed outside the past, as taḍribu “you hit”, wa-iḍrib “and hit!” and wa-lā taḍrib “and do not hit!”.

text.original: وَيَاءُ تَضْرِبِينَ عَلَامَةٌ لِلْخِطَابِ، وَالْفَاعِلُ مُسْتَتِرٌ عِنْدَ الْأَخْفَشِ، وَعِنْدَ الْعَامَّةِ هِيَ ضَمِيرٌ بَارِزٌ لِلْفَاعِلِ، كَوَاوِ يَضْرِبُونَ، وَعُيِّنَ الْيَاءُ لِمَجِيئِهِ فِي: هَذِي أَمَةُ اللَّهِ، لِلتَّأْنِيثِ.
text.en: The yāʾ of taḍribīna “you (f.) hit” is a sign of address, and the fāʿil is hidden, according to al-Akhfash; according to most, it is a visible pronoun of the fāʿil, like the wāw of yaḍribūna “they hit”. The yāʾ was chosen because it comes for the feminine in hadhī amatu Allāhi “this is the handmaid of God”.

text.original: وَلَمْ يُزَدْ فِي تَضْرِبِينَ مِنْ حُرُوفِ أَنْتِ لِلِالْتِبَاسِ بِالتَّثْنِيَةِ فِي زِيَادَةِ الْأَلِفِ، وَاجْتِمَاعِ النُّونَيْنِ فِي النُّونِ، وَتَكْرَارِ التَّاءَيْنِ فِي التَّاءِ، وَأُبْرِزَ الْيَاءُ لِلْفَرْقِ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ جَمْعِهِ، وَلَمْ يُفْرَقْ بِحَرَكَةِ مَا قَبْلَ النُّونِ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِالنُّونِ الثَّقِيلَةِ فِي الصُّورَةِ، وَلَا تُحْذَفُ النُّونُ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِالْمُذَكَّرِ الْمُخَاطَبِ فِي الْمُضَارِعِ.
text.en: None of the letters of anti “you (f.)” was added in taḍribīna: [not the alif] because of confusion with the dual if the alif were added, [not the nūn] because two nūns would come together in the nūn, and [not the tāʾ] because two tāʾs would be repeated in the tāʾ. The yāʾ was made visible to distinguish it from its plural; it was not distinguished by the vowel of what is before the nūn, so that it is not confused in its look with the heavy nūn; and the nūn is not dropped, so that it is not confused with the man addressed in the muḍāriʿ.

lessons.title: Why the pronoun hides, and where it must
body: The last two places of the hidden pronoun: the speaker, aḍribu and naḍribu, and the adjective, ḍāribun, ḍāribāni, ḍāribūna. Then the reasons. It hides in the marfūʿ and not in the object or the jarr pronoun “because it stands as a part of the verb”. It hides in the absent singular, not in the dual and plural, “because hiding is light, and giving the light to the singular, which comes first, is more fitting”.

Why not in the past's speaker and person addressed (ḍarabtu, ḍarabta)? “Hiding is a weak indication and being visible a strong one”, and the speaker and the person addressed, who are present, are strong: the strong pronoun goes to the strong persons. In the future they hide all the same, “for the distinction”: aḍribu and taḍribu, with nothing added, are kept apart from the past.

Another view says it hides wherever something else points to it: the bare form in ḍaraba, the tāʾ in ḍarabat, the yāʾ of yaḍribu, the tāʾ of taḍribu, the hamza of aḍribu, the nūn of naḍribu, and the adjective's own form. These prefixes “are letters, not nouns”: they show the person without being the pronoun.

Two proofs follow. The tāʾ of ḍarabat cannot be a pronoun like the tāʾ of ḍarabta, because it stays when an explicit doer follows: ḍarabat Hindun, “Hind hit”; a pronoun and a named doer would be two doers. The alif of ḍāribāni cannot be a pronoun, “because it changes in naṣb and jarr” (ḍāribayni), while a pronoun does not change, as the alif of yaḍribāni stays alif in every state.

Last, where hiding is necessary: afʿalu, tafʿalu, ifʿal, nafʿalu, “because the form indicates it”. You may put a named doer after yaḍribu or ḍaraba, but afʿalu Zaydun, “I do, Zayd”, is “ugly”: the hamza already says “I”, and no noun can take its place. So hiding is necessary with “I”, “we” and “you”, and only allowed with “he” and “she”.

terms.en: necessary hiding: afʿalu, tafʿalu, ifʿal, nafʿalu
making the pronoun visible: the strong indication
the indication that points to a hidden pronoun
the prefixes of the future: letters, not pronouns

examples.en: aḍribu, naḍribu: the hidden pronoun of the speaker
ḍarabat Hindun: the tāʾ stays beside a named doer, so it is no pronoun
afʿalu Zaydun: “ugly”, for the form itself says “I”

tasks.prompt: Prove that the tāʾ of ḍarabat is not a pronoun.
tasks.answer: It stays when a named feminine doer follows: ḍarabat Hindun. If it were the doer's pronoun, the sentence would have two doers, the tāʾ and Hind. So it is only a sign of the feminine.

tasks.prompt: Prove that the alif of ḍāribāni is not a pronoun, but the alif of yaḍribāni is.
tasks.answer: The alif of ḍāribāni changes in naṣb and jarr (ḍāribayni), so it is a case ending; a pronoun never changes, as the alif of yaḍribāni stays an alif in every state.

tasks.prompt: Why is the pronoun visible in ḍarabtu but hidden in aḍribu?
tasks.answer: In the past the speaker, a strong person, is given the strong indication, a visible pronoun. In the future the pronoun hides for the distinction: the hamza of aḍribu already shows the speaker, and the form differs from the past.

tasks.prompt: Why is afʿalu Zaydun ugly, while ḍarabat Hindun is good?
tasks.answer: In afʿalu the hiding is necessary: the hamza shows “I”, and no named doer can replace the pronoun. In ḍarabat the hiding is only allowed: the pronoun “she” may give way to a named doer.

quiz.prompt: Why does the pronoun hide in the marfūʿ only?
options: It stands as a part of the verb
quiz.explanation: The doer's pronoun is bound to the verb.

quiz.prompt: Why does it hide in the singular and not in the dual and plural?
options: Hiding is light, and the light goes to the singular, which comes first
quiz.explanation: The singular comes first and gets the lighter treatment.

quiz.prompt: Why is the pronoun visible in ḍarabta?
options: The strong person addressed gets the strong indication
quiz.explanation: Visibility is the strong indication.

quiz.prompt: Ḍarabat Hindun proves that the tāʾ of ḍarabat is…
quiz.explanation: It is not dropped beside a named doer.

quiz.prompt: The alif of ḍāribāni is no pronoun because…
options: it changes in naṣb and jarr
quiz.explanation: Ḍāribayni; a pronoun does not change.

quiz.prompt: Hiding is necessary in…
quiz.explanation: The form indicates it; no named doer can stand there.

quiz.prompt: The prefixes of aḍribu and naḍribu are…
quiz.explanation: They point to the hidden pronoun without being it.

text.original: وَفِي الْمُتَكَلِّمِ، نَحْوُ: أَضْرِبُ وَنَضْرِبُ، وَفِي الصِّفَةِ، نَحْوُ: ضَارِبٌ وَضَارِبَانِ وَضَارِبُونَ إِلَى آخِرِهِ. وَاسْتَتَرَ فِي الْمَرْفُوعِ دُونَ الْمَنْصُوبِ وَالْمَجْرُورِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ بِمَنْزِلَةِ جُزْءِ الْفِعْلِ، وَاسْتَتَرَ فِي الْغَائِبِ وَالْغَائِبَةِ دُونَ التَّثْنِيَةِ وَالْجَمْعِ؛ لِأَنَّ الِاسْتِتَارَ خَفِيفٌ، فَإِعْطَاءُ الْخَفِيفِ لِلْمُفْرَدِ السَّابِقِ أَوْلَى، دُونَ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ وَالْمُخَاطَبِ اللَّذَيْنِ فِي الْمَاضِي؛ لِأَنَّ الِاسْتِتَارَ قَرِينَةٌ ضَعِيفَةٌ، وَالْإِبْرَازَ قَرِينَةٌ قَوِيَّةٌ، فَإِعْطَاءُ الْإِبْرَازِ الْقَوِيِّ لِلْمُتَكَلِّمِ الْقَوِيِّ وَالْمُخَاطَبِ الْقَوِيِّ أَوْلَى، وَاسْتَتَرَ فِي مُخَاطَبِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ وَمُتَكَلِّمِهِ لِلْفَرْقِ.
text.en: And in the speaker, as aḍribu “I hit” and naḍribu “we hit”; and in the adjective, as ḍāribun, ḍāribāni and ḍāribūna “hitting” to its end. It is hidden in the marfūʿ, not in the manṣūb and the majrūr, because it stands as a part of the verb. It is hidden in the absent man and the absent woman, not in the dual and the plural, because hiding is light, and giving the light to the singular, which comes first, is more fitting; [and] not in the speaker and the man addressed that are in the past, because hiding is a weak indication and being visible a strong one, so giving the strong visibility to the strong speaker and the strong man addressed is more fitting. It is hidden in the man addressed of the future and in its speaker, for the distinction.

text.original: وَقِيلَ: يَسْتَتِرُ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَوَاضِعِ لِوُجُودِ الدَّلِيلِ، وَهُوَ عَدَمُ الْإِبْرَازِ فِي مِثْلِ: ضَرَبَ، وَالتَّاءُ فِي مِثْلِ: ضَرَبَتْ، وَالْيَاءُ فِي مِثْلِ: يَضْرِبُ، وَالتَّاءُ فِي مِثْلِ: تَضْرِبُ، وَالْهَمْزَةُ فِي مِثْلِ: أَضْرِبُ، وَالنُّونُ فِي مِثْلِ: نَضْرِبُ، وَهِيَ حُرُوفٌ لَيْسَتْ بِأَسْمَاءٍ، وَالصِّفَةُ فِي مِثْلِ: ضَارِبٌ وَضَارِبَانِ وَضَارِبُونَ.
text.en: It is also said: it is hidden in these places because there is an indication of it: the absence of a visible [pronoun] in the like of ḍaraba; the tāʾ in the like of ḍarabat; the yāʾ in the like of yaḍribu; the tāʾ in the like of taḍribu; the hamza in the like of aḍribu; the nūn in the like of naḍribu — and these are letters, not nouns —; and the adjective in the like of ḍāribun, ḍāribāni and ḍāribūna.

text.original: وَلَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ تَاءُ ضَرَبَتْ ضَمِيرًا كَتَاءِ ضَرَبْتَ؛ لِوُجُودِ عَدَمِ حَذْفِهَا بِالْفَاعِلَةِ الظَّاهِرَةِ، نَحْوُ: ضَرَبَتْ هِنْدٌ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ أَلِفُ ضَارِبَانِ ضَمِيرًا؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَتَغَيَّرُ فِي حَالَةِ النَّصْبِ وَالْجَرِّ، وَالضَّمِيرُ لَا يَتَغَيَّرُ، كَأَلِفِ يَضْرِبَانِ. وَالِاسْتِتَارُ وَاجِبٌ فِي مِثْلِ: أَفْعَلُ وَتَفْعَلُ وَافْعَلْ وَنَفْعَلُ؛ لِدَلَالَةِ الصِّيغَةِ عَلَيْهِ، وَقَبُحَ: أَفْعَلُ زَيْدٌ، وَتَفْعَلُ زَيْدٌ، وَافْعَلْ زَيْدٌ، وَنَفْعَلُ زَيْدُونَ.
text.en: The tāʾ of ḍarabat cannot be a pronoun like the tāʾ of ḍarabta, because it is not dropped with an explicit feminine fāʿil, as ḍarabat Hindun “Hind hit”; and the alif of ḍāribāni cannot be a pronoun, because it changes in the state of naṣb and jarr, and a pronoun does not change, like the alif of yaḍribāni “they two hit”. Hiding is necessary in the like of afʿalu, tafʿalu, ifʿal and nafʿalu, because the form indicates it; and afʿalu Zaydun, tafʿalu Zaydun, ifʿal Zaydun and nafʿalu Zaydūna are ugly.

lessons.title: Mustaqbal and muḍāriʿ, and the letters of atayna
body: The future “too comes in fourteen forms, as yaḍribu to its end”. It has two names. Mustaqbal, “future”, because the future is in its meaning. Muḍāriʿ, “resembling”, because it resembles ḍārib, the active participle: in its vowels and sukūns (ya-ḍ-ri-bu like ḍā-ri-bun: a vowel, a quiescent letter, two vowels), in describing an indefinite noun, and in taking the lām of beginning: inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun, “Zayd is surely standing”, wa-la-yaqūmu, “and will surely stand”.

It resembles the generic noun as well. Rajul, “a man”, is general, and al-rajul, “the man”, is made particular by the lām of the known; yaḍribu is general, present or future, and is made particular by sa- or sawfa, “will”. And it resembles a word like ʿayn, which has many meanings, in being shared between two times: yaḍribu is “he hits” and “he will hit”.

To make it, “the letters of atayna were added to the past”: alif, tāʾ, yāʾ and nūn. Letters, not separate words, because a word of one letter would be below “the proper measure”. At the beginning, because at the end they would look like the past's own endings (ḍarabta, ḍarabnā). It is made from the past because the past “indicates firmness”: what has happened is fixed. And the additions go to the future, not to the past, because the augmented comes after the bare as the future comes after the past: “the preceding was given to the preceding”.

Each letter has its reason, drawn from the map of the mouth. The alif (hamza) for the speaker: it comes from the furthest point of the throat, where speech begins, and the speaker begins speech; or it agrees with anā. The wāw for the person addressed: it comes from the lips, where speech ends, and speech ends with the one who hears it; then it was changed into a tāʾ, so that wāws would not pile up in wa-wawjalu, “and you fear”. The yāʾ, from the middle of the mouth, for the absent, who stands between speaker and hearer. The nūn for “we”, as in ḍarabnā; or because the weak letters were used up, and the nūn, sounding through the nose, is near them.

From the wāw comes a rule worth keeping: “the first letter of a word is not fit for the addition of a wāw”, so if a word begins with a wāw, that wāw is a root letter, as in warantal, “calamity”. Such reasons are aids to understanding: they tie each prefix to something already known.

terms.en: the future: this book's name for the imperfect
the resembling: the imperfect, named for its likeness to the participle
the four prefixes: alif, tāʾ, yāʾ, nūn
the lām of beginning, “surely”, taken by nouns and by the muḍāriʿ
the proper measure of a word

examples.en: inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun wa-la-yaqūmu: the lām of beginning on the participle and on the muḍāriʿ
wa-wawjalu: the wāws that would have piled up, hence the tāʾ
warantal: a word whose first wāw is a root letter

tasks.prompt: Give three ways in which yaḍribu resembles ḍārib.
tasks.answer: In its vowels and sukūns (a vowel, a quiescent letter, then two vowels); in describing an indefinite noun; and in taking the lām of beginning (inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun, wa-la-yaqūmu).

tasks.prompt: Why were the prefixes put at the beginning and not at the end?
tasks.answer: At the end they would be confused with the past, whose persons are marked by endings (ḍarabta, ḍarabnā).

tasks.prompt: Match each prefix to its person, with the book's reason.
tasks.answer: Alif (hamza): the speaker, because it comes from the furthest point of the throat, where speech begins (or to agree with anā). Tāʾ, from wāw: the person addressed, because the wāw comes from the lips, where speech ends. Yāʾ: the absent, because it comes from the middle of the mouth, as the absent stands between. Nūn: “we”, as in ḍarabnā.

tasks.prompt: How does yaḍribu, which can mean “he hits” or “he will hit”, become future only?
tasks.answer: With sa- or sawfa, as a general noun is made particular by the lām of the known: rajul, al-rajul.

quiz.prompt: The name muḍāriʿ means…
quiz.explanation: It resembles the active participle ḍārib.

quiz.prompt: Which is NOT a resemblance of yaḍribu to ḍārib?
quiz.explanation: Ḍārib begins with its root letter; the other three are the book's.

quiz.prompt: The letters added to make the future are those of…
quiz.explanation: Alif, tāʾ, yāʾ, nūn.

quiz.prompt: Why was the alif chosen for the speaker?
options: It comes from where speech begins, the depth of the throat
quiz.explanation: The speaker begins speech; or it agrees with anā.

quiz.prompt: The tāʾ of taḍribu was originally…
quiz.explanation: Changed so that wāws would not pile up, as in wa-wawjalu.

quiz.prompt: What makes yaḍribu particular to the future?
quiz.explanation: As the article makes a generic noun particular.

quiz.prompt: The wāw at the start of warantal is…
quiz.explanation: The first letter of a word is not fit for an added wāw.

text.original: وَهُوَ أَيْضًا يَجِيءُ عَلَى أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ وَجْهًا، نَحْوُ: يَضْرِبُ إِلَى آخِرِهِ. وَيُقَالُ لَهُ: مُسْتَقْبَلٌ؛ لِوُجُودِ مَعْنَى الِاسْتِقْبَالِ فِي مَعْنَاهُ، وَيُقَالُ لَهُ: مُضَارِعٌ؛ لِأَنَّهُ مُشَابِهٌ بِضَارِبٍ فِي الْحَرَكَاتِ وَالسَّكَنَاتِ، وَفِي وُقُوعِهِ صِفَةً لِلنَّكِرَةِ، وَفِي دُخُولِ لَامِ الِابْتِدَاءِ، نَحْوُ: إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَقَائِمٌ وَلَيَقُومُ، وَبِاسْمِ الْجِنْسِ فِي الْعُمُومِ وَالْخُصُوصِ، يَعْنِي: أَنَّ اسْمَ الْجِنْسِ يَخْتَصُّ بِلَامِ الْعَهْدِ كَمَا يَخْتَصُّ يَضْرِبُ بِالسِّينِ أَوْ سَوْفَ، وَبِالْعَيْنِ فِي الِاشْتِرَاكِ بَيْنَ الْحَالِ وَالِاسْتِقْبَالِ.
text.en: It too comes in fourteen forms, as yaḍribu “he hits” to its end. It is called mustaqbal (“future”) because the meaning of the future is found in its meaning; and it is called muḍāriʿ (“resembling”) because it resembles ḍāribin “hitting” in its vowels and sukūns, in coming as an adjective of an indefinite, and in the entering of the lām of beginning, as inna Zaydan la-qāʾimun “Zayd is surely standing” and wa-la-yaqūmu “and will surely stand”; and it resembles the generic noun in being general and particular — that is, the generic noun is made particular by the lām of the known, as yaḍribu is made particular by the sīn or sawfa; and it resembles [the word] ʿayn in being shared, [here] between the present and the future.

text.original: زِيدَتْ عَلَى الْمَاضِي حُرُوفُ أَتَيْنَ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ مُسْتَقْبَلًا؛ لِأَنَّ بِتَقْدِيرِ الِانْفِصَالِ يَصِيرُ أَقَلَّ مِنَ الْقَدْرِ الصَّالِحِ، وَزِيدَتْ فِي الْأَوَّلِ دُونَ الْآخِرِ؛ لِأَنَّ فِي الْآخِرِ يَلْتَبِسُ بِالْمَاضِي، وَاشْتُقَّ مِنَ الْمَاضِي؛ لِأَنَّ الْمَاضِيَ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الثَّبَاتِ، وَزِيدَتْ فِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ دُونَ الْمَاضِي؛ لِأَنَّ الْمَزِيدَ عَلَيْهِ بَعْدَ الْمُجَرَّدِ، وَالْمُسْتَقْبَلَ بَعْدَ الزَّمَانِ الْمَاضِي، فَأُعْطِيَ السَّابِقُ لِلسَّابِقِ، وَاللَّاحِقُ لِلَّاحِقِ.
text.en: The letters of atayna (alif, tāʾ, yāʾ, nūn) were added to the past so that it becomes a future, because, taken as a separate [word], it would be less than the proper measure. They were added at the beginning, not at the end, because at the end it would be confused with the past. It was derived from the past because the past indicates firmness. They were added in the future, not in the past, because what is augmented comes after the bare, and the future comes after past time; so the preceding was given to the preceding, and the following to the following.

text.original: وَعُيِّنَتِ الْأَلِفُ لِلْمُتَكَلِّمِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْأَلِفَ مِنْ أَقْصَى الْحَلْقِ، وَهُوَ مَبْدَأُ الْمَخَارِجِ، وَالْمُتَكَلِّمُ هُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الْكَلَامَ، وَقِيلَ: لِلْمُوَافَقَةِ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ أَنَا. وَعُيِّنَتِ الْوَاوُ لِلْمُخَاطَبِ؛ لِكَوْنِهِ مِنْ مُنْتَهَى الْمَخَارِجِ، وَالْمُخَاطَبُ هُوَ الَّذِي يَنْتَهِي الْكَلَامُ بِهِ، ثُمَّ قُلِبَتِ الْوَاوُ تَاءً حَتَّى لَا تَجْتَمِعَ الْوَاوَاتُ فِي نَحْوِ: وَوَوْجَلُ فِي الْعَطْفِ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ قِيلَ: الْأَوَّلُ مِنْ كُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ لَا يَصْلُحُ لِزِيَادَةِ الْوَاوِ، وَحُكِمَ أَنَّ وَاوَ وَرَنْتَلٍ أَصْلٌ.
text.en: The alif was chosen for the speaker because the alif is from the furthest part of the throat, which is the beginning of the points of articulation, and the speaker is the one who begins speech; and it is said: for agreement between it and anā “I”. The wāw was chosen for the man addressed because it is from the end of the points of articulation, and the man addressed is the one with whom speech ends; then the wāw was changed into a tāʾ so that wāws do not come together, in the like of wawawjalu with the wāw of joining. For this reason it is said: the first [letter] of a word is not fit for the addition of a wāw; and it was judged that the wāw of warantalin “calamity” is original.

text.original: وَعُيِّنَتِ الْيَاءُ لِلْغَائِبِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْيَاءَ مِنْ وَسَطِ الْفَمِ، وَالْغَائِبُ هُوَ الَّذِي يَكُونُ فِي وَسَطِ الْكَلَامِ بَيْنَ الْمُتَكَلِّمِ وَالْمُخَاطَبِ. وَعُيِّنَتِ النُّونُ لِلْمُتَكَلِّمِ إِذَا كَانَ مَعَهُ غَيْرُهُ؛ لِتَعَيُّنِهَا لِذَلِكَ فِي ضَرَبْنَا، وَقِيلَ: زِيدَتِ النُّونُ؛ لِأَنَّهُ لَمْ يَبْقَ مِنْ حُرُوفِ الْعِلَّةِ شَيْءٌ، وَهُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْ حُرُوفِ الْعِلَّةِ فِي خُرُوجِهَا عَنْ هَوَاءِ الْخَيْشُومِ.
text.en: The yāʾ was chosen for the absent because the yāʾ is from the middle of the mouth, and the absent is the one who is in the middle of speech, between the speaker and the man addressed. The nūn was chosen for the speaker when another is with him, because it was chosen for that in ḍarabnā; and it is said: the nūn was added because nothing remained of the letters of weakness, and it is near the letters of weakness in coming out with the air of the nose.

lessons.title: The vowel of the prefix, and the double tāʾ
body: “These letters were given a fatḥa for lightness, except in the quadriliteral”: in the four patterns whose past has four letters, faʿlala, afʿala, faʿʿala and fāʿala, the prefix takes a ḍamma: yudaḥriju, yukrimu, yuqaṭṭiʿu, yuqātilu. The reason given: these four are quadriliteral, the quadriliteral is a branch of the triliteral, “and the ḍamma too is a branch of the fatḥa”: the branch for the branch. Or: because they are less used. The longer patterns go back to fatḥa “because their letters are many”, and a heavy ḍamma would weigh them down: yatafaḍḍalu, yastakhriju.
Yuharīqu, “he pours out”, looks like a five-letter verb with a ḍamma, but “its origin is yurīqu”, from the four-letter arāqa, and the hāʾ “was added against the rule”: the ḍamma belongs to afʿala.

Some dialects put a kasra on the prefixes when the past has a kasra on its ʿayn or on its hamza, “so that they indicate the kasra of the past”: yiʿlamu, tiʿlamu, iʿlamu, niʿlamu for ʿalima; yistanṣiru for istanṣara. Some of these spare the yāʾ, “because the kasra is heavy on the yāʾ”. Why the prefix and not a root letter? A kasra on the fāʾ would give a run of vowels; on the ʿayn it would blur yafʿalu and yafʿilu; on the lām it would wipe out the iʿrāb.

Last, tataqalladu, tatabāʿadu, tatabakhtaru: the second tāʾ “is dropped”, because two like letters meet and cannot be assimilated, and so these are said with a single tāʾ, as in the Qurʾān's tanazzalu al-malāʾikatu (97:4) for tatanazzalu. The second goes, not the first, “because the first is a sign, and a sign is not dropped”: the first tāʾ shows the person.

For practice: the prefix of a sound verb is fatḥa everywhere except in the four-letter group, where it is ḍamma. The conjugation tool follows this; the kasra of yiʿlamu is a dialect the madrasa knows but does not recite.

the branch for the branch: the ḍamma for the quadriliteral
a sign is not dropped

tasks.prompt: Which prefixes take a ḍamma, and what reasons does the book give?
tasks.answer: Those of the four patterns with four letters in the past: faʿlala, afʿala, faʿʿala, fāʿala (yudaḥriju, yukrimu, yuqaṭṭiʿu, yuqātilu). The quadriliteral is a branch of the triliteral and the ḍamma a branch of the fatḥa; or, they are less used.

tasks.prompt: Why do the five- and six-letter patterns have fatḥa on the prefix?
tasks.answer: Because their letters are many, and the heavy ḍamma would weigh down a long word; the light fatḥa suits them.

tasks.prompt: Why does a dialect put the kasra on the prefix of yiʿlamu, and not on a root letter?
tasks.answer: To point to the kasra of the past ʿalima. On the fāʾ it would make a run of vowels, on the ʿayn it would confuse yafʿalu with yafʿilu, and on the lām it would cancel the iʿrāb; the prefix, being added, can carry it.

tasks.prompt: In tataqalladu, which tāʾ is dropped, and why that one?
tasks.answer: The second. The first is a sign of the person (the prefix), and a sign is not dropped.

quiz.prompt: The prefix of yukrimu has a ḍamma because akrama is…
quiz.explanation: Its past has four letters, like daḥraja.

quiz.prompt: Which future has a fatḥa on its prefix?
quiz.explanation: Istakhraja has many letters, so the light fatḥa.

quiz.prompt: The origin of yuharīqu is…
quiz.explanation: The hāʾ was added against the rule.

quiz.prompt: In which dialect form does the prefix take a kasra?
quiz.explanation: It points to the kasra of ʿalima.

quiz.prompt: Why would a kasra on the ʿayn not do in that dialect?
options: It would confuse yafʿalu with yafʿilu
It would make a run of vowels
It is heavy on the yāʾ
quiz.explanation: Each root letter is ruled out with its own reason.

quiz.prompt: In tataqalladu, the tāʾ dropped is…
quiz.explanation: The first is a sign, and a sign is not dropped.

quiz.prompt: “The branch for the branch” pairs…
quiz.explanation: The quadriliteral is a branch of the triliteral, the ḍamma of the fatḥa.

text.original: وَفُتِحَتْ هَذِهِ الْحُرُوفُ لِلْخِفَّةِ إِلَّا فِي الرُّبَاعِيِّ، وَهُوَ فَعْلَلَ وَأَفْعَلَ وَفَعَّلَ وَفَاعَلَ؛ لِأَنَّ هَذِهِ الْأَرْبَعَةَ رُبَاعِيَّةٌ، وَالرُّبَاعِيُّ فَرْعٌ لِلثُّلَاثِيِّ، وَالضَّمُّ أَيْضًا فَرْعٌ لِلْفَتْحِ، وَقِيلَ: لِقِلَّةِ اسْتِعْمَالِهِنَّ، وَفُتِحَ مَا وَرَاءَهُنَّ لِكَثْرَةِ حُرُوفِهِنَّ. وَأَمَّا يُهَرِيقُ فَأَصْلُهُ يُرِيقُ، وَهُوَ مِنَ الرُّبَاعِيِّ، فَزِيدَتِ الْهَاءُ عَلَى خِلَافِ الْقِيَاسِ.
text.en: These letters were given a fatḥa for lightness, except in the quadriliteral, which is faʿlala, afʿala, faʿʿala and fāʿala: because these four are quadriliteral, and the quadriliteral is a branch of the triliteral, and the ḍamma too is a branch of the fatḥa; and it is said: because they are little used. What is beyond them was given a fatḥa because their letters are many. As for yuharīqu “he pours out”, its origin is yurīqu, which is from the quadriliteral, and the hāʾ was added against the rule.

text.original: وَتُكْسَرُ حُرُوفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ فِي بَعْضِ اللُّغَةِ إِذَا كَانَ مَاضِيهِ مَكْسُورَ الْعَيْنِ أَوْ مَكْسُورَةَ الْهَمْزَةِ حَتَّى تَدُلَّ عَلَى كَسْرَةِ الْمَاضِي، نَحْوُ: يِعْلَمُ وَتِعْلَمُ وَإِعْلَمُ وَنِعْلَمُ، وَيِسْتَنْصِرُ وَتِسْتَنْصِرُ وَإِسْتَنْصِرُ وَنِسْتَنْصِرُ، وَفِي بَعْضِ اللُّغَةِ لَا يُكْسَرُ الْيَاءُ لِثِقَلِ الْكَسْرَةِ عَلَى الْيَاءِ.
text.en: In some dialects the letters of the muḍāriʿ take a kasra when its past has a kasra on the ʿayn, or has a kasra on the hamza, so that they indicate the kasra of the past, as yiʿlamu, wa-tiʿlamu, wa-iʿlamu and wa-niʿlamu “he knows, and you know, and I know, and we know”, and yistanṣiru, wa-tistanṣiru, wa-istanṣiru and wa-nistanṣiru “he asks for help, and you, and I, and we ask for help”; and in some dialects the yāʾ does not take a kasra, because the kasra is heavy on the yāʾ.

text.original: وَعُيِّنَتْ حُرُوفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ لِلدَّلَالَةِ عَلَى كَسْرَةِ الْعَيْنِ فِي الْمَاضِي؛ لِأَنَّهَا زَائِدَةٌ، وَقِيلَ: لِأَنَّهُ يَلْزَمُ بِكَسْرِ الْفَاءِ تَوَالِي الْحَرَكَاتِ، وَبِكَسْرِ الْعَيْنِ يَلْزَمُ الِالْتِبَاسُ بَيْنَ يَفْعَلُ وَيَفْعِلُ، وَبِكَسْرِ اللَّامِ يَلْزَمُ إِبْطَالُ الْإِعْرَابِ. وَتُحْذَفُ التَّاءُ الثَّانِيَةُ فِي مِثْلِ: تَتَقَلَّدُ وَتَتَبَاعَدُ وَتَتَبَخْتَرُ؛ لِاجْتِمَاعِ الْحَرْفَيْنِ مِنْ جِنْسٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَعَدَمِ إِمْكَانِ الْإِدْغَامِ، وَعُيِّنَتِ الثَّانِيَةُ لِلْحَذْفِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْأُولَى عَلَامَةٌ، وَالْعَلَامَةُ لَا تُحْذَفُ.
text.en: The letters of the muḍāriʿ were chosen to indicate the kasra of the ʿayn in the past because they are added; and it is said: because with a kasra on the fāʾ a succession of vowels would be required, with a kasra on the ʿayn confusion between yafʿalu and yafʿilu would be required, and with a kasra on the lām the cancelling of iʿrāb would be required. The second tāʾ is dropped in the like of tataqalladu “you gird yourself”, tatabāʿadu “you keep away” and tatabakhtaru “you strut”, because two letters of one kind come together and assimilation is not possible; and the second was chosen for dropping because the first is a sign, and a sign is not dropped.

lessons.title: The quiescent fāʾ, the shared form, and the nūn of rafʿ
body: In yaḍribu the fāʾ is quiescent, “fleeing from a succession of vowels”: with the prefix, ya-ḍa-ri-bu would be four vowels in a row. Why silence the fāʾ? Because the run “arose from the yāʾ”, the added letter, and the fitting letter to quiet is the one next to it. The same reasoning picked the bāʾ of ḍarabna (lesson 8): it stands next to the nūn that caused the run.

Taḍribu serves for “you (a man)” and for “she”. The two were made the same in the future “because they are the same in the past”: naṣarta and naṣarat both carry a tāʾ. For “she” the tāʾ could not be quiescent, for one cannot begin with a quiescent letter; nor take a ḍamma, which would make it look passive (tumdaḥu, “she is praised”); nor a kasra, which would make it look like the dialect of tiʿlamu. “If it is said: the fatḥa confuses too” (with “you”), the answer is that the fatḥa agrees with its sisters yaḍribu, aḍribu, naḍribu, and is light.

In yaḍribāni, yaḍribūna and taḍribīna a nūn is put at the end “as a sign of rafʿ”. The reason: once the doer's pronoun (-ā, -ū, -ī) is attached, the end of the verb “has come to stand as the middle of the word”, and the middle of a word cannot show iʿrāb. So the nūn shows it, and the nūn goes when the verb is in naṣb or jazm.

Not so the nūn of yaḍribna: it is “a sign of the feminine, as in faʿalna”, not of rafʿ, and it stays in every state. That is also why the women's plural takes the prefix yāʾ, yaḍribna, and not the tāʾ of “she”: two signs of the feminine must not meet. The yāʾ of taḍribīna, by contrast, is the doer's pronoun.

Last: “when lam enters the future its meaning moves to the past”: lam yaḍrib, “he did not hit”. Lam resembles a word of condition, which moves a past form into the future; lam moves in the other direction.

terms.en: the nūn that marks rafʿ in the five verbs: -āni, -ūna, -īna
the nūn of the women: a sign of the feminine, never dropped
a run of vowels, avoided by silencing the fāʾ
the particle that puts the future in jazm and turns its meaning to the past

examples.en: naṣarta, naṣarat: alike in the past, so taḍribu is shared in the future
tumdaḥu, “she is praised”: why the tāʾ of “she” has no ḍamma
yaḍribna: the nūn a sign of the feminine, with the prefix yāʾ

tasks.prompt: Why is the fāʾ of yaḍribu quiescent, and why the fāʾ rather than another letter?
tasks.answer: To avoid four vowels in a row (ya-ḍa-ri-bu). The run arose from the added yāʾ, so the letter next to it, the fāʾ, is the fitting one to make quiescent.

tasks.prompt: Why does the tāʾ of “she” in taḍribu have a fatḥa, of all vowels?
tasks.answer: It cannot be quiescent (one cannot begin with it), a ḍamma would look passive (tumdaḥu), a kasra would look like the dialect of tiʿlamu; the fatḥa agrees with yaḍribu, aḍribu and naḍribu and is light, so it is kept even though “you” has the same form.

tasks.prompt: Put yaḍribūna and yaḍribna after lan, using the conjugation tool, and explain the difference.
tasks.answer: Lan yaḍribū and lan yaḍribna. The nūn of yaḍribūna is the sign of rafʿ, so it drops in naṣb; the nūn of yaḍribna is the sign of the feminine and stays.

quiz.explanation: The run arose from the prefix, so the letter next to it was silenced.

quiz.explanation: Hence the fatḥa.

quiz.explanation: The verb's end has become like the middle of the word, so the nūn shows the iʿrāb.

quiz.explanation: As in faʿalna; it is never dropped.

quiz.explanation: The nūn is already a feminine sign.

quiz.explanation: Lam moves the meaning of the future to the past.

text.original: وَأُسْكِنَتِ الْفَاءُ فِي مِثْلِ: يَضْرِبُ فِرَارًا عَنْ تَوَالِي الْحَرَكَاتِ، وَعُيِّنَتِ الْفَاءُ لِلسُّكُونِ؛ لِأَنَّ تَوَالِيَ الْحَرَكَاتِ لَزِمَ مِنَ الْيَاءِ، فَإِسْكَانُ الْحَرْفِ الَّذِي هُوَ قَرِيبٌ مِنْهُ أَوْلَى، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ عُيِّنَتِ الْبَاءُ فِي ضَرَبْنَ لِلْإِسْكَانِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ النُّونِ الَّذِي لَزِمَ مِنْهُ تَوَالِي الْحَرَكَاتِ.
text.en: The fāʾ was made unvowelled in the like of yaḍribu, fleeing from a succession of vowels; and the fāʾ was chosen for the sukūn because the succession of vowels arose from the yāʾ, so making unvowelled the letter that is near it is more fitting. For this reason the bāʾ in ḍarabna was chosen to be made unvowelled, because it is near the nūn, from which the succession of vowels arose.

text.original: وَسُوِّيَ بَيْنَ الْمُخَاطَبِ وَالْغَائِبَةِ فِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ لِاسْتِوَائِهِمَا فِي الْمَاضِي، نَحْوُ: نَصَرْتَ وَنَصَرَتْ، وَلَكِنْ لَا يُسَكَّنُ فِي غَائِبَةِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ لِضَرُورَةِ الِابْتِدَاءِ، وَلَا يُضَمُّ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِالْمَجْهُولِ فِي تُمْدَحُ، وَلَا يُكْسَرُ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِلُغَةِ تِعْلَمُ. فَإِنْ قِيلَ: يَلْزَمُ الِالْتِبَاسُ أَيْضًا فِي الْفَتْحَةِ، قُلْنَا: إِذًا فِي الْفَتْحَةِ مُوَافَقَةٌ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَ أَخَوَاتِهَا مَعَ خِفَّةِ الْفَتْحَةِ.
text.en: The man addressed and the absent woman were made the same in the future because they are the same in the past, as naṣarta “you helped” and naṣarat “she helped”. But [the first letter] is not made unvowelled in the absent woman of the future, because one must begin [with a vowel]; nor is it given a ḍamma, so that it is not confused with the passive in tumdaḥu “she is praised”; nor a kasra, so that it is not confused with the dialect of tiʿlamu. If it is said: confusion is also required with the fatḥa, we say: with the fatḥa there is agreement between it and its sisters, together with the lightness of the fatḥa.

text.original: وَأُدْخِلَ فِي آخِرِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ نُونٌ عَلَامَةٌ لِلرَّفْعِ؛ لِأَنَّ آخِرَ الْفِعْلِ صَارَ بِاتِّصَالِ ضَمِيرِ الْفَاعِلِ بِمَنْزِلَةِ وَسَطِ الْكَلِمَةِ، إِلَّا نُونَ يَضْرِبْنَ، وَهِيَ عَلَامَةٌ لِلتَّأْنِيثِ كَمَا فِي فَعَلْنَ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ يُقَالُ بِالْيَاءِ حَتَّى لَا يَجْتَمِعَ عَلَامَتَا التَّأْنِيثِ، وَالْيَاءُ فِي تَضْرِبِينَ ضَمِيرُ الْفَاعِلِ كَمَا مَرَّ. وَإِذَا دَخَلَ لَمْ عَلَى الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ يَنْتَقِلُ مَعْنَاهُ إِلَى الْمَاضِي؛ لِأَنَّهُ مُشَابِهٌ بِكَلِمَةِ الشَّرْطِ.
text.en: A nūn was put at the end of the future as a sign of rafʿ, because by the attaching of the pronoun of the fāʿil the end of the verb has come to stand as the middle of the word — except the nūn of yaḍribna “they (f.) hit”, which is a sign of the feminine, as in faʿalna; for this reason it is said with the yāʾ, so that two signs of the feminine do not come together. The yāʾ in taḍribīna is the pronoun of the fāʿil, as has passed. When lam enters the future its meaning moves to the past, because it resembles a word of condition.

lessons.title: The command of the absent, and of the one addressed
body: “The command is a form by which the act is sought from the doer.” It begins with the absent: li-yaḍrib, li-yaḍribā, li-yaḍribū, li-taḍrib, li-taḍribā, li-yaḍribna, “let him hit … let them (women) hit”. It is derived from the muḍāriʿ, because both look to the future.

Why a lām? It comes “from the middle of the points of articulation”, and it is one of the letters of addition, the letters that may be added to a root, which a line of verse gathers: hawītu al-simāna, “I loved the plump ones”. No weak letter was chosen, so that two weak letters would not meet with the prefix yāʾ.

The lām has a kasra “because it resembles the lām of jarr”, li-Zaydin: jazm in verbs “stands as jarr in nouns”. After wa- and fa- it becomes quiescent, wa-lyaḍrib, fa-lyaḍrib, as fakhidh, “thigh”, may be said with a quiescent khāʾ, and wa-huwa as wa-hwa. Watch for this when reading: the lām of the command often hides behind a wa or a fa.

For the person addressed “the letter of the future was dropped”: taḍrib loses its tāʾ, and with a hamza of joining (next lesson) becomes iḍrib. This marks his command off from the absent's, and the dropping went to him “because it is much used”: one commands the person in front of one far more often. That is why the passive command keeps everything, li-tuḍrab, “be hit!”: it is little used, so nothing is shortened.

So the command has two shapes: the long one, lām with the jussive, for the absent and for what is rare; and the short one, the jussive without its prefix, for the person addressed. The Kūfans think the short one is the long one worn down (lesson 20).

terms.en: the lām of the command: li-yaḍrib
the command of the absent: “let him …”
the command of the one addressed: iḍrib
the letters of addition, gathered in hawītu al-simāna

examples.en: hawītu al-simāna: the line that gathers the letters of addition
wa-lyaḍrib, fa-lyaḍrib: the lām quiescent after wa and fa
li-tuḍrab, “be hit!”: the passive command keeps its prefix

tasks.answer: Because it resembles the lām of jarr: jazm in verbs stands as jarr in nouns, so the lām that brings jazm takes the vowel of the lām that brings jarr.

tasks.answer: Fa- with the lām of the command, made quiescent after the fa (as fakhidh can be said with a quiescent khāʾ): “so let him hit”.

tasks.answer: It is dropped to tell the command of the one addressed from the absent's, and the dropping went to it because it is much used. The passive command is little used, so it keeps the lām and the prefix.

text.original: الْأَمْرُ صِيغَةٌ يُطْلَبُ بِهَا الْفِعْلُ عَنِ الْفَاعِلِ، نَحْوُ: لِيَضْرِبْ لِيَضْرِبَا لِيَضْرِبُوا لِتَضْرِبْ لِتَضْرِبَا لِيَضْرِبْنَ، وَهُوَ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنَ الْمُضَارِعِ لِمُنَاسَبَةٍ بَيْنَهُمَا فِي الِاسْتِقْبَالِيَّةِ.
text.en: The command is a form by which the act is sought from the doer, as li-yaḍrib li-yaḍribā li-yaḍribū li-taḍrib li-taḍribā li-yaḍribna “let him hit, let the two of them hit, let them hit, let her hit, let the two of them (f.) hit, let them (f.) hit”. It is derived from the muḍāriʿ because of a correspondence between them in futurity.

text.original: زِيدَتِ اللَّامُ فِي الْغَائِبِ؛ لِأَنَّهَا مِنْ وَسَطِ الْمَخَارِجِ، وَأَيْضًا مِنْ حُرُوفِ الزَّوَائِدِ، وَهِيَ الَّتِي يَشْتَمِلُهَا قَوْلُ الشَّاعِرِ: هَوِيتُ السِّمَانَ فَشَيَّبْنَنِي * وَقَدْ كُنْتُ قِدْمًا هَوِيتُ السِّمَانَا، أَيْ: حُرُوفُ «هَوِيتُ السِّمَانَ». وَلَمْ يُزَدْ مِنْ حُرُوفِ الْعِلَّةِ حَتَّى لَا يَجْتَمِعَ حَرْفَا عِلَّةٍ، وَكُسِرَتِ اللَّامُ؛ لِأَنَّهَا مُشَابِهَةٌ بِاللَّامِ الْجَارَّةِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْجَزْمَ فِي الْأَفْعَالِ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْجَرِّ فِي الْأَسْمَاءِ، وَأُسْكِنَتْ بِالْوَاوِ وَالْفَاءِ، نَحْوُ: وَلْيَضْرِبْ فَلْيَضْرِبْ، كَمَا أُسْكِنَ فِي فَخِذٍ، وَنَظِيرُهُ فِي الْوَاوِ: وَهْوَ.
text.en: The lām was added in the absent because it is from the middle of the points of articulation, and also one of the letters of addition, which are those that the poet's saying contains: hawītu al-simāna fa-shayyabnanī / wa-qad kuntu qidman hawītu al-simānā “I loved the plump ones and they made me grey; and long ago I had loved the plump ones”, that is, the letters of hawītu al-simāna. None of the letters of weakness was added, so that two letters of weakness do not come together. The lām was given a kasra because it resembles the lām of jarr, since jazm in verbs stands as jarr in nouns; and it was made unvowelled after the wāw and the fāʾ, as wa-lyaḍrib and fa-lyaḍrib “and let him hit”, as [the khāʾ] is made unvowelled in fakhidhin “thigh”; its like with the wāw is wa-hwa “and he”.

text.original: وَحُذِفَتْ حَرْفُ الِاسْتِقْبَالِ فِي الْمُخَاطَبِ لِلْفَرْقِ بَيْنَ أَمْرِ الْمُخَاطَبِ وَأَمْرِ الْغَائِبِ، وَعُيِّنَ الْحَذْفُ فِي الْمُخَاطَبِ لِكَثْرَةِ الِاسْتِعْمَالِ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ لَا تُحْذَفُ مَعَ اللَّامِ فِي مَجْهُولِهِ، أَعْنِي: يُقَالُ: لِتُضْرَبْ؛ لِقِلَّةِ اسْتِعْمَالِهِ.
text.en: The letter of the future was dropped in the man addressed, to distinguish the command of the man addressed from the command of the absent; dropping was chosen in the man addressed because it is much used. For this reason it is not dropped [but kept] with the lām in its passive; I mean, one says li-tuḍrab “be hit!”, because it is little used.

lessons.title: The hamza of joining
body: With the prefix gone, taḍrib leaves ḍrib, and Arabic does not begin a word with a quiescent letter. So “a hamza is brought in for beginning when what follows it is unvowelled”: iḍrib. It is a hamza of joining (waṣl): said when you begin with the word, dropped when the word is joined to what goes before. It has a kasra “because the kasra is the origin in the hamzas of joining”.

Not in uktub, “write!”: there it has a ḍamma, because i-k-tu would go from a kasra to a ḍamma. But a quiescent kāf stands between them! “With them an unvowelled letter is not a strong barrier”, and the book proves it from qinwa, “acquisition”, which became qinya: the kasra of the qāf changed the wāw across the quiescent nūn. Others simply say the hamza follows the ḍamma of the ʿayn.

Three alifs take a fatḥa. Aymun, in oaths, though a hamza of joining: it began as the plural of yamīn, “oath”, and the alif of such plurals is a hamza of cutting (qaṭʿ); frequent use then made it joining. The article al-, for its frequency too. And akrim, “honour!”, because its alif is no hamza of the command at all: it is the hamza of cutting of afʿala, which dropped from tuʾakrimu “because of the meeting of the two hamzas in uʾakrimu”, and returns in the command. So akrim is said with its hamza even inside a sentence.

In writing, the alif of joining stays even where it is not said, so that iʿlam, “know!”, is not taken for ʿallim, “teach!”. One could tell them apart by the marks, “but the marks are often left out”; for the same reason the wāw of ʿAmr is written to tell it from ʿUmar. It is left out in bismi Allāhi, because the phrase is much used, but kept in iqraʾ bi-ismi rabbika (96:1), which is less used.

The rule to keep: a command whose letter after the prefix is quiescent takes a hamza of joining, with a ḍamma if the ʿayn has a ḍamma (uktub, unṣur), otherwise a kasra (iḍrib, iʿlam). A command whose letter after the prefix has a vowel takes none: qaṭṭiʿ, qātil, daḥrij. Akrim is the one with a hamza of cutting.

terms.en: the hamza of joining: said at the start, dropped inside speech
the hamza of cutting: always said, as in akrim
following: a vowel taken to match a neighbouring vowel
a strong barrier: what a quiescent letter is not
the marks (dots and signs) that tell letters and forms apart

examples.en: qinwa becoming qinya: the quiescent nūn no barrier to the kasra
tuʾakrimu, uʾakrimu: the origins in which the hamza of afʿala stood
ʿUmar and ʿAmr, told apart in writing by the wāw
unṣur, iḍrib, qaṭṭiʿ: hamza with ḍamma, with kasra, and none (conjugation tool)

tasks.prompt: Why does uktub have a ḍamma on its hamza, though a quiescent kāf stands between the hamza and the ḍamma?
tasks.answer: A kasra would make the word go from a kasra to a ḍamma (i-k-tu), and a quiescent letter is not a strong barrier between them, as qinwa shows, which became qinya across a quiescent nūn. So the hamza takes a ḍamma (or, others say, it simply follows the ḍamma of the ʿayn).

tasks.prompt: Why is the alif of akrim said even in the middle of a sentence, unlike that of iḍrib?
tasks.answer: The alif of akrim is the hamza of cutting of the pattern afʿala, which had dropped from tukrimu (from tuʾakrimu) and comes back in the command; the alif of iḍrib is a hamza of joining, brought in only to begin.

tasks.prompt: Why is the alif of joining kept in writing?
tasks.answer: So that iʿlam, the command of ʿalima, is not taken for ʿallim, the command of ʿallama; the marks that would tell them apart are often left out.

tasks.prompt: Which of these commands begin with a hamza of joining: unṣur, qaṭṭiʿ, iḍrib, akrim? Use the conjugation tool.
tasks.answer: Unṣur (with ḍamma) and iḍrib (with kasra) begin with a hamza of joining. Qaṭṭiʿ needs none, its first letter having a vowel; akrim has the hamza of cutting of afʿala.

quiz.prompt: Why is a hamza brought in for iḍrib?
options: One cannot begin with a quiescent letter
quiz.explanation: After the prefix drops, the ḍād is quiescent.

quiz.prompt: The origin in the hamza of joining is…
quiz.explanation: So iḍrib, iʿlam.

quiz.prompt: Uktub takes a ḍamma because…
options: the kāf is a throat letter
a kasra would go to a ḍamma across a weak barrier
quiz.explanation: A quiescent letter is no strong barrier.

quiz.prompt: Qinya from qinwa proves that…
options: the wāw is a root letter
a quiescent letter is no strong barrier
quiz.explanation: The kasra acted on the wāw across the nūn.

quiz.prompt: The alif of akrim is…
quiz.explanation: It is the hamza of afʿala, dropped from tukrimu and back in the command.

quiz.prompt: Why is aymun said with a fatḥa?
options: It was the plural of yamīn, whose alif was of cutting
quiz.explanation: Frequent use then made it a hamza of joining.

quiz.prompt: Where is the alif of ism left out in writing?
quiz.explanation: Because bismi Allāhi is much used.

text.original: وَاجْتُلِبَتِ الْهَمْزَةُ بَعْدَ حَذْفِ حَرْفِ الْمُضَارَعَةِ إِذَا كَانَ مَا بَعْدَهُ سَاكِنًا لِلِافْتِتَاحِ، وَكُسِرَتِ الْهَمْزَةُ؛ لِأَنَّ الْكَسْرَةَ أَصْلٌ فِي هَمَزَاتِ الْوَصْلِ، وَلَمْ يُكْسَرْ فِي مِثْلِ: اكْتُبْ؛ لِأَنَّ بِتَقْدِيرِ الْكَسْرِ يَلْزَمُ الْخُرُوجُ مِنَ الْكَسْرَةِ إِلَى الضَّمَّةِ، وَلَا اعْتِبَارَ لِلْكَافِ السَّاكِنِ؛ لِأَنَّ السَّاكِنَ لَا يَكُونُ حَاجِزًا حَصِينًا عِنْدَهُمْ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ جُعِلَ وَاوُ قِنْوَةٍ يَاءً، وَيُقَالُ: قِنْيَةٌ، وَقِيلَ: تُضَمُّ لِلْإِتْبَاعِ.
text.en: After the letter of the muḍāriʿ is dropped, a hamza is brought in for beginning when what follows it is unvowelled; and the hamza was given a kasra because the kasra is the origin in the hamzas of joining (hamzat al-waṣl). It was not given a kasra in the like of uktub “write!”, because with a kasra going from a kasra to a ḍamma would be required; and the unvowelled kāf is not taken into account, because with them an unvowelled letter is not a strong barrier: for this reason the wāw of qinwatin “acquisition” was made a yāʾ, and one says qinyatun. It is also said: it takes a ḍamma for following [the ḍamma].

text.original: وَفُتِحَ أَلِفُ أَيْمُنٍ مَعَ كَوْنِهِ لِلْوَصْلِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ جَمْعُ يَمِينٍ، وَالْأَلِفُ فِي الْجَمْعِ لِلْقَطْعِ، ثُمَّ جُعِلَ لِلْوَصْلِ لِكَثْرَةِ اسْتِعْمَالِهِ، وَفُتِحَ أَلِفُ التَّعْرِيفِ لِكَثْرَتِهِ أَيْضًا. وَفُتِحَ أَلِفُ أَكْرِمْ؛ لِأَنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَلِفِ الْأَمْرِ، بَلْ أَلِفُ الْقَطْعِ، فَحُذِفَ مِنْ تُؤَكْرِمُ لِاجْتِمَاعِ الْهَمْزَتَيْنِ فِي أُؤَكْرِمُ.
text.en: The alif of aymunin “oaths” was given a fatḥa though it is for joining, because it is the plural of yamīnin “oath”, and the alif in the plural is for cutting (qaṭʿ); then it was made for joining because it is much used. The alif of the definite article was given a fatḥa because it too is frequent. The alif of akrim “honour!” was given a fatḥa because it is not the alif of the command but an alif of cutting; it was dropped from tuʾakrimu because of the meeting of the two hamzas in uʾakrimu.

text.original: وَلَا تُحْذَفُ أَلِفُ الْوَصْلِ فِي الْخَطِّ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ عَلِمَ بِأَمْرِ عَلَّمَ، فَإِنْ قِيلَ: يُعْلَمُ بِالْإِعْجَامِ، قُلْنَا: الْإِعْجَامُ يُتْرَكُ كَثِيرًا، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ فَرَّقُوا بَيْنَ عُمَرَ وَعَمْرٍو بِالْوَاوِ، وَحُذِفَ فِي بِسْمِ اللَّهِ لِكَثْرَةِ الِاسْتِعْمَالِ، وَلَا تُحْذَفُ فِي ﴿اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ﴾ لِقِلَّةِ اسْتِعْمَالِهِ.
text.en: The alif of joining is not dropped in writing, so that the command of ʿalima “to know” is not confused with the command of ʿallama “to teach”. If it is said: it is known by the marks (iʿjām), we say: the marks are often left out; for this reason they distinguished ʿUmara and ʿAmrin by the wāw. It was dropped in bismi Allāhi “in the name of God” because it is much used, and it is not dropped in iqraʾ bi-ismi rabbika “read in the name of your Lord” [96:1] because it is little used.

lessons.title: Is the command in jazm or built?
body: The command of the absent, li-yaḍrib, is in jazm by the lām “by agreement”: the lām “resembles a word of condition in moving” the meaning, and words of condition bring jazm. The command of the one addressed, iḍrib, is the question.

The Kūfans say it is in jazm too, because its origin is li-taḍrib. They point to a reading of the Prophet: fa-bi-dhālika fa-ltafraḥū, “in that, then, rejoice” (10:58), with the lām and the tāʾ of the person addressed. The steps, as they tell it: the lām was dropped because it is much used; then the prefix was dropped to tell the command from the muḍāriʿ; the ḍād was left quiescent, so a hamza of joining was brought in, put in the place of the prefix and given its effect, the jazm.

Can a letter keep the work of a word that has gone? Yes, they answer, as in a line of Imruʾ al-Qays: fa-mithliki ḥublā qad ṭaraqtu, “many a one like you, pregnant, have I visited by night”: mithliki is in jarr by rubba, “many a”, which is not there; the fa- that took its place does its work.

The Baṣrans say iḍrib is built (mabnī): “the origin in verbs is being built”, and the muḍāriʿ is inflected only because it resembles the noun. Drop the prefix of the muḍāriʿ and the resemblance is gone, and the iʿrāb with it. They accept the reading fa-ltafraḥū as inflected, for there the prefix, the cause of iʿrāb, is still present.

Note what the two sides share: the form. Both say iḍrib, iḍribā, iḍribū, iḍribī, iḍribna, shaped exactly as the jussive of the person addressed without its prefix. They differ only in naming the ending: the effect of a governor (jazm), or a fixed ending (bināʾ). Lesson 7 has already given the Baṣran view: the command is built on the sukūn.

terms.en: the jussive case of the verb, brought by a governor
being built: a fixed ending that no governor brings
a word of condition, which brings jazm
“many a”: a particle of jarr that can work while left unsaid

examples.en: li-taḍrib: the origin of iḍrib, for the Kūfans
fa-bi-dhālika fa-ltafraḥū: the reading the Kūfans cite
fa-mithliki ḥublā qad ṭaraqtu: jarr by a rubba not said

tasks.prompt: Give the Kūfans' steps from li-taḍrib to iḍrib.
tasks.answer: The lām was dropped because it is much used (taḍrib); the prefix was dropped to tell the command from the muḍāriʿ (ḍrib, with a quiescent ḍād); a hamza of joining was brought in, in the place of the prefix, and given its effect, the jazm: iḍrib.

tasks.prompt: What is the Baṣrans' argument that iḍrib is built?
tasks.answer: The origin in verbs is bināʾ; the muḍāriʿ is inflected only because it resembles the noun, a resemblance that rests on its prefix. Iḍrib has lost the prefix, so the resemblance and the iʿrāb are gone.

tasks.prompt: Why do the Baṣrans accept fa-ltafraḥū as inflected?
tasks.answer: Because it keeps the prefix tāʾ, the cause of iʿrāb; it is a command with the lām, inflected like li-yaḍrib.

quiz.explanation: The lām resembles a word of condition.

quiz.explanation: Worn down by dropping the lām and the prefix.

quiz.explanation: With the lām and the tāʾ of the person addressed.

quiz.explanation: As the fa- carries the work of rubba.

text.original: وَيُجْزَمُ آخِرُهُ فِي الْغَائِبِ بِاللَّامِ إِجْمَاعًا؛ لِأَنَّ اللَّامَ مُشَابِهَةٌ بِكَلِمَةِ الشَّرْطِ فِي النَّقْلِ، وَكَذَلِكَ الْمُخَاطَبُ عِنْدَ الْكُوفِيِّينَ؛ لِأَنَّ أَصْلَ اضْرِبْ لِتَضْرِبْ عِنْدَهُمْ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ قَرَأَ النَّبِيُّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْتَفْرَحُوا﴾.
text.en: Its end is put in jazm by the lām in the absent, by agreement, because the lām resembles a word of condition in moving [the meaning]; and likewise the man addressed, according to the Kūfans, because according to them the origin of iḍrib “hit!” is li-taḍrib. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, recited: fa-bi-dhālika fa-ltafraḥū “in that, then, rejoice” [10:58].

text.original: حُذِفَ اللَّامُ لِكَثْرَةِ الِاسْتِعْمَالِ، ثُمَّ حُذِفَتْ عَلَامَةُ الِاسْتِقْبَالِ لِلْفَرْقِ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْمُضَارِعِ، فَبَقِيَ الضَّادُ سَاكِنًا، وَاجْتُلِبَتْ هَمْزَةُ الْوَصْلِ، وَوُضِعَتْ مَوْضِعَ عَلَامَةِ الِاسْتِقْبَالِ، وَأُعْطِيَ لَهُ أَثَرُ عَلَامَةِ الِاسْتِقْبَالِ، كَمَا أُعْطِيَ لِفَاءِ رُبَّ عَمَلُ رُبَّ فِي مِثْلِ قَوْلِ الشَّاعِرِ: فَمِثْلِكِ حُبْلَى قَدْ طَرَقْتُ وَمُرْضِعٍ * فَأَلْهَيْتُهَا عَنْ ذِي تَمَائِمَ مُحْوِلِ.
text.en: The lām was dropped because it is much used; then the sign of the future was dropped to distinguish it from the muḍāriʿ, so the ḍād remained unvowelled; the hamza of joining was brought in and put in the place of the sign of the future, and it was given the effect of the sign of the future, as the fāʾ of rubba was given the work of rubba in the like of the poet's saying: fa-mithliki ḥublā qad ṭaraqtu wa-murḍiʿin / fa-alhaytuhā ʿan dhī tamāʾima muḥwili “many a one like you, pregnant or nursing, have I visited by night, and made her forget her year-old child with his amulets”.

text.original: وَعِنْدَ الْبَصْرِيِّينَ مَبْنِيٌّ؛ لِأَنَّ الْأَصْلَ فِي الْأَفْعَالِ الْبِنَاءُ، وَإِنَّمَا أُعْرِبَ الْمُضَارِعُ لِمُشَابَهَةٍ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الِاسْمِ، وَلَمْ يَبْقَ الْمُشَابَهَةُ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْأَمْرِ بِحَذْفِ حَرْفِ الْمُضَارَعَةِ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ قِيلَ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَلْتَفْرَحُوا﴾ مُعْرَبٌ بِالْإِجْمَاعِ؛ لِوُجُودِ عِلَّةِ الْإِعْرَابِ، وَهِيَ حَرْفُ الْمُضَارَعَةِ.
text.en: According to the Baṣrans it is mabnī, because the origin in verbs is being mabnī, and the muḍāriʿ was given iʿrāb only because of a resemblance between it and the noun; and with the dropping of the letter of the muḍāriʿ the resemblance does not remain between it and the command. For this reason it is said: His saying fa-ltafraḥū “then rejoice” is muʿrab by agreement, because the cause of iʿrāb, the letter of the muḍāriʿ, is found.

lessons.title: The two nūns of emphasis
body: “The two nūns of emphasis were added at the end of the command to emphasise the request”: the heavy nūn, -nna, and the light, -n. The print gives the heavy nūn in full, for the absent (li-yaḍribanna … li-yaḍribnānni) and for the person addressed (iḍribanna … iḍribnānni). Learn the six forms of the one addressed as a row: -anna, -ānni, -unna, -inna, -ānni, -nānni.

Each vowel has its cause. In li-yaḍribanna the bāʾ takes a fatḥa, “fleeing from the meeting of two unvowelled letters” (b and n), and the nūn has a fatḥa “for lightness”. The wāw of the plural drops, “the ḍamma being enough”: li-yaḍribunna; the yāʾ of the woman drops, “the kasra being enough”: iḍribinna. The alif of the dual stays, “so that it is not confused with the singular”: li-yaḍribānni.

After that alif the heavy nūn takes a kasra, “because it resembles the nūn of the dual”, -āni. The nūn of rafʿ drops before it: hal taḍribānni, not taḍribānanni, “because what is before the heavy nūn becomes built”. And in the women's plural a “separating alif” is put between the two nūns, li-yaḍribnānni, “fleeing from the meeting of nūns”.

The light nūn follows the same rules, except that it never comes after the two alifs (the dual's and the separating one): a long ā followed by a single quiescent n would bring “two unvowelled letters” together “outside their proper bound”. Yūnus allowed it, by analogy with the heavy one.

Both nūns come in seven places, wherever there is “the meaning of request”: the command; the prohibition, lā taḍribanna, “do not hit!”; the question, hal taḍribanna, “will you hit?”; the wish, laytaka taḍribanna; the offer, alā taḍribanna, “won't you hit?”; the oath, wa-Allāhi la-aḍribanna, “by God, I will hit”; and, rarely, the negation. The prohibition is like the command in everything, “except that it is inflected by agreement”.

terms.en: the heavy nūn of emphasis: -nna
the light nūn of emphasis: -n
the separating alif of -nānni
the meeting of two quiescent letters
an early Baṣran grammarian, who allowed the light nūn after the alif

examples.en: hal taḍribānni: the nūn of rafʿ dropped before the heavy nūn
li-yaḍribnānni: the separating alif between the nūns
laytaka taḍribanna: emphasis with a wish
wa-Allāhi la-aḍribanna: emphasis with an oath

tasks.prompt: Explain the vowel before the nūn in iḍribanna, iḍribunna and iḍribinna.
tasks.answer: Iḍribanna: the bāʾ takes a fatḥa to avoid two quiescent letters meeting. Iḍribunna: the wāw of the plural (iḍribū) dropped, the ḍamma being enough to show it. Iḍribinna: the yāʾ of the woman (iḍribī) dropped, the kasra being enough.

tasks.prompt: Why does the dual keep its alif, iḍribānni, and why is the nūn there with a kasra?
tasks.answer: The alif stays so that the dual is not confused with the singular iḍribanna. The heavy nūn after it takes a kasra because it then resembles the nūn of the dual, -āni.

tasks.prompt: Name the seven places where the nūns of emphasis come, with the book's examples.
tasks.answer: The command (iḍribanna); the prohibition (lā taḍribanna); the question (hal taḍribanna); the wish (laytaka taḍribanna); the offer (alā taḍribanna); the oath (wa-Allāhi la-aḍribanna); and, rarely, the negation (lā taḍribanna, “you will not hit”).

tasks.prompt: Why can the light nūn not be added to the dual or to the women's plural?
tasks.answer: There it would follow an alif (of the dual, or the separating alif), and a long ā followed by a single quiescent nūn is a meeting of two quiescent letters outside their allowed bound. Yūnus allowed it by analogy with the heavy nūn.

options: What comes before the heavy nūn is built, so the nūn of rafʿ goes
quiz.explanation: The verb before the nūn becomes mabnī.

quiz.explanation: The separating alif.

options: The plain statement of a past act
quiz.explanation: They come where there is a sense of request; the past is not among them.

text.original: وَزِيدَتْ فِي آخِرِ الْأَمْرِ نُونَا التَّأْكِيدِ لِتَأْكِيدِ الطَّلَبِ، نَحْوُ: لِيَضْرِبَنَّ لِيَضْرِبَانِّ لِيَضْرِبُنَّ لِتَضْرِبَنَّ لِتَضْرِبَانِّ لِيَضْرِبْنَانِّ، وَكَذَلِكَ فِي: اضْرِبَنَّ اضْرِبَانِّ اضْرِبُنَّ اضْرِبِنَّ اضْرِبَانِّ اضْرِبْنَانِّ. وَفُتِحَ الْبَاءُ فِي لِيَضْرِبَنَّ فِرَارًا عَنِ اجْتِمَاعِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ، وَفُتِحَ النُّونُ لِلْخِفَّةِ، وَحُذِفَ وَاوُ لِيَضْرِبُوا اكْتِفَاءً بِالضَّمَّةِ، وَيَاءُ اضْرِبِي اكْتِفَاءً بِالْكَسْرَةِ، وَلَمْ يُحْذَفْ أَلِفُ التَّثْنِيَةِ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِالْوَاحِدِ.
text.en: The two nūns of emphasis were added at the end of the command to emphasise the request, as li-yaḍribanna li-yaḍribānni li-yaḍribunna li-taḍribanna li-taḍribānni li-yaḍribnānni “let him (the two of them, them, her, the two of them f., them f.) surely hit”; and likewise in iḍribanna iḍribānni iḍribunna iḍribinna iḍribānni iḍribnānni “surely hit!” (to a man, two, men, a woman, two women, women). The bāʾ in li-yaḍribanna was given a fatḥa, fleeing from the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and the nūn a fatḥa for lightness. The wāw of li-yaḍribū was dropped, the ḍamma being enough, and the yāʾ of iḍribī “hit! (f.)”, the kasra being enough; the alif of the dual was not dropped, so that it is not confused with the singular.

text.original: وَكُسِرَ النُّونُ الثَّقِيلَةُ بَعْدَ أَلِفِ التَّثْنِيَةِ؛ لِأَنَّهَا مُشَابِهَةٌ بِنُونِ التَّثْنِيَةِ، وَحُذِفَ النُّونُ الَّتِي هِيَ تَدُلُّ عَلَى الرَّفْعِ فِي مِثْلِ: هَلْ تَضْرِبَانِّ؛ لِأَنَّ مَا قَبْلَ النُّونِ الثَّقِيلَةِ يَصِيرُ مَبْنِيًّا، وَأُدْخِلَ الْأَلِفُ الْفَاصِلَةُ فِي مِثْلِ: لِيَضْرِبْنَانِّ فِرَارًا عَنِ اجْتِمَاعِ النُّونَاتِ.
text.en: The heavy nūn takes a kasra after the alif of the dual because it resembles the nūn of the dual. The nūn that indicates rafʿ was dropped in the like of hal taḍribānni “will you two surely hit?”, because what is before the heavy nūn becomes mabnī. The separating alif was put in, in the like of li-yaḍribnānni, fleeing from the meeting of nūns.

text.original: وَحُكْمُ الْخَفِيفَةِ مِثْلُ حُكْمِ الثَّقِيلَةِ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ لَا تَدْخُلُ بَعْدَ الْأَلِفَيْنِ لِاجْتِمَاعِ السَّاكِنَيْنِ عَلَى غَيْرِ حَدِّهِ، وَعِنْدَ يُونُسَ تَدْخُلُ قِيَاسًا عَلَى الثَّقِيلَةِ.
text.en: The rule of the light [nūn] is like the rule of the heavy, except that it does not enter after the two alifs, because two unvowelled letters would meet outside their proper bound; according to Yūnus it enters, by analogy with the heavy.

text.original: وَكِلَاهُمَا تَدْخُلَانِ فِي سَبْعَةِ مَوَاضِعَ لِوُجُودِ مَعْنَى الطَّلَبِ فِيهَا: الْأَمْرُ كَمَا مَرَّ، وَالنَّهْيُ، نَحْوُ: لَا تَضْرِبَنَّ، وَالِاسْتِفْهَامُ، نَحْوُ: هَلْ تَضْرِبَنَّ، وَالتَّمَنِّي، نَحْوُ: لَيْتَكَ تَضْرِبَنَّ، وَالْعَرْضُ، نَحْوُ: أَلَا تَضْرِبَنَّ، وَالْقَسَمُ، نَحْوُ: وَاللَّهِ لَأَضْرِبَنَّ، وَالنَّفْيُ قَلِيلًا لِمُشَابَهَتِهِ بِالنَّهْيِ، نَحْوُ: لَا تَضْرِبَنَّ. وَالنَّهْيُ مِثْلُ الْأَمْرِ فِي جَمِيعِ الْوُجُوهِ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُ مُعْرَبٌ بِالْإِجْمَاعِ.
text.en: Both of them enter in seven places, because the meaning of request is found in them: the command, as has passed; the prohibition, as lā taḍribanna “do not hit!”; the question, as hal taḍribanna “will you hit?”; the wish, as laytaka taḍribanna “would that you hit”; the offer, as alā taḍribanna “will you not hit?”; the oath, as wa-Allāhi la-aḍribanna “by God, I will surely hit”; and negation, rarely, because it resembles prohibition, as lā taḍribanna “you will not hit”. The prohibition is like the command in all respects, except that it is muʿrab by agreement.

lessons.title: The passive
body: “The passive comes from the things mentioned”: from the past, ḍuriba, “he was hit”, and from the future, yuḍrabu, “he is hit”, through all their persons. Why leave the doer unnamed? “For the lowliness of the doer, or his greatness, or his being well known”: he is not worth naming, too great to name, or known to all.

The passive past has the form fuʿila, a ḍamma then a kasra, “because its meaning is not of the usual kind”: it gives the act to the one who suffers it. So it was given a form “not of the usual kind” too: no noun has the pattern fuʿil “except wuʿil and duʾil”, the mountain goat and the weasel. The future is yufʿalu, which is like fuʿila in its vowels and sukūns, and no noun has it either.

In the augmented patterns, “like akrama”, the passive past has a ḍamma on the first letter and a kasra before the last, ukrima; the future a ḍamma on the first and a fatḥa before the last, yukramu, “following the triliteral”.

“Except in seven patterns”, where the first vowelled letter takes a ḍamma along with the first letter: tufuʿʿila, tufūʿila, uftuʿila, unfuʿila, ufʿulla (the print is unclear here; this is our reading), ustufʿila and ufʿūʿila. In the first two the fāʾ takes a ḍamma so that they are not confused with the futures of faʿʿala and fāʿala. In the five with a hamza of joining, the tāʾ (or first vowelled letter) takes a ḍamma so that the passive is not confused with the command in pause: with a fatḥa, wa-ftaʿil (passive) and wa-ftaʿil (command) would sound alike.

The conjugation tool gives these passives: tafaḍḍala, tufuḍḍila; taḍāraba, tuḍūriba, with the alif said as ū after the ḍamma; iḥtaqara, uḥtuqira; istakhraja, ustukhrija. Inṣarafa, which takes no object, has no passive in the tool, though the book names its pattern unfuʿila.

terms.en: the passive: “the unknown”, the verb whose doer is not named
the pattern of the passive past
the pattern of the passive future
the first vowelled letter, which takes a ḍamma in seven patterns

wuʿil and duʾil: the only nouns on fuʿil
