tasks.prompt: Give three reasons for leaving the doer unnamed, as the book lists them.
tasks.answer: The doer's lowliness, his greatness, or his being well known.

tasks.prompt: Why was the passive past given the unusual form fuʿila?
tasks.answer: Because its meaning is unusual: the act is attributed to the one it falls on. So its form is unusual too: no noun has the pattern fuʿil except wuʿil and duʾil.

tasks.prompt: Make the passive past of tafaḍḍala and istakhraja (conjugation tool) and say which letters take the ḍamma and why.
tasks.answer: Tufuḍḍila: the tāʾ and the fāʾ, so that it is not confused with the future of faḍḍala. Ustukhrija: the first vowelled letter, the tāʾ, with the hamza of joining, so that it is not confused with the command in pause.

quiz.prompt: The passive of ḍaraba is…
quiz.explanation: Fuʿila: a ḍamma, then a kasra before the last.

quiz.prompt: Which is NOT a reason the book gives for leaving the doer unnamed?
quiz.explanation: The three reasons are lowliness, greatness and fame.

quiz.prompt: Why does no noun have the pattern fuʿil, with two exceptions?
options: The pattern was kept unusual for the unusual passive
quiz.explanation: Wuʿil and duʾil are the only nouns.

quiz.prompt: The passive future of ḍaraba is…
quiz.explanation: Yufʿalu: a ḍamma on the prefix, a fatḥa before the last.

quiz.prompt: In ukrima, which letter has the ḍamma?
options: the first vowelled letter after a hamza of joining
quiz.explanation: Afʿala takes the ḍamma on its first letter only.

quiz.prompt: Why does the fāʾ of tufuḍḍila take a ḍamma?
options: Not to be confused with the command
Not to be confused with the future of faʿʿala
quiz.explanation: Tufaḍḍila would look like tufaḍḍilu.

quiz.prompt: In ustukhrija the ḍamma on the tāʾ prevents confusion with…
quiz.explanation: With a fatḥa, the passive and the command would sound alike in pause.

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ الْمَجْهُولُ مِنَ الْأَشْيَاءِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ: مِنَ الْمَاضِي، نَحْوُ: ضُرِبَ إِلَى آخِرِهِ، وَمِنَ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ، نَحْوُ: يُضْرَبُ إِلَى آخِرِهِ، وَالْغَرَضُ مِنْ وَضْعِهِ إِمَّا لِخَسَاسَةِ الْفَاعِلِ، أَوْ لِعَظَمَتِهِ، أَوْ لِشُهْرَتِهِ. وَاخْتُصَّ بِصِيغَةِ فُعِلَ فِي الْمَاضِي؛ لِأَنَّ مَعْنَاهُ غَيْرُ مَعْقُولٍ، وَهُوَ إِسْنَادُ الْفِعْلِ إِلَى الْمَفْعُولِ، فَجُعِلَ صِيغَتُهُ أَيْضًا غَيْرَ مَعْقُولَةٍ، وَهِيَ فُعِلَ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ لَا يَجِيءُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الصِّيغَةِ كَلِمَةٌ إِلَّا وُعِلٌ وَدُئِلٌ.
text.en: The passive comes from the things mentioned: from the past, as ḍuriba “he was hit” to its end, and from the future, as yuḍrabu “he is hit” to its end. The aim in making it is the lowliness of the doer, or his greatness, or his being well known. In the past it was given the form fuʿila alone, because its meaning, the attributing of the act to the object, is not of the usual kind, so its form too was made one not of the usual kind, which is fuʿila; for this reason no word comes on this form except wuʿilun “mountain goat” and duʾilun “weasel”.

text.original: وَفِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ عَلَى يُفْعَلُ؛ لِأَنَّ هَذِهِ الصِّيغَةَ مِثْلُ فُعِلَ فِي الْحَرَكَاتِ وَالسَّكَنَاتِ، وَلَا يَجِيءُ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةٌ أَيْضًا. وَيَجِيءُ فِي الزَّوَائِدِ مِنَ الثُّلَاثِيِّ كَأَكْرَمَ بِضَمِّ الْأَوَّلِ وَكَسْرِ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ فِي الْمَاضِي، وَبِضَمِّ الْأَوَّلِ وَفَتْحِ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ فِي الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ، تَبَعًا لِلثُّلَاثِيِّ.
text.en: In the future [it comes] on yufʿalu, because this form is like fuʿila in its vowels and sukūns, and no word comes on it either. In the augmented [forms] of the triliteral, like akrama, it comes with a ḍamma on the first [letter] and a kasra on what is before the last in the past, and with a ḍamma on the first and a fatḥa on what is before the last in the future, following the triliteral.

text.original: إِلَّا فِي سَبْعَةِ أَبْوَابٍ، فَإِنَّ أَوَّلَ الْمُتَحَرِّكِ يُضَمُّ مَعَ ضَمِّ الْأَوَّلِ فِيهَا، وَيُكْسَرُ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ، وَهِيَ: تُفُعِّلَ، وَتُفُوعِلَ، وَافْتُعِلَ، وَانْفُعِلَ، وَافْعُلَّ، وَاسْتُفْعِلَ، وَافْعُوعِلَ. وَضُمَّ الْفَاءُ فِي الْأَوَّلَيْنِ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَا بِمُضَارِعَيْ فَعَّلَ وَفَاعَلَ، وَضُمَّ أَوَّلُ الْمُتَحَرِّكِ فِي الْخَمْسَةِ الْبَاقِيَةِ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِالْأَمْرِ فِي الْوَقْفِ؛ إِذَا قُلْتَ: وَافْتَعِلْ، بِفَتْحِ التَّاءِ فِي الْمَجْهُولِ فِي الْوَقْفِ بِوَصْلِ الْهَمْزَةِ، وَافْتَعِلْ فِي الْأَمْرِ، يَلْزَمُ الِالْتِبَاسُ، فَضُمَّ التَّاءُ لِإِزَالَتِهِ، فَقِسِ الْبَاقِيَ عَلَيْهِ.
text.en: Except in seven patterns: in them the first vowelled [letter] takes a ḍamma together with the ḍamma of the first, and what is before the last takes a kasra. They are tufuʿʿila, tufūʿila, uftuʿila, unfuʿila, ufʿulla, ustufʿila and ufʿūʿila. The fāʾ was given a ḍamma in the first two so that they are not confused with the muḍāriʿs of faʿʿala and fāʿala; and the first vowelled [letter] in the five remaining was given a ḍamma so that it is not confused with the command in pause: if you say wa-iftaʿil with a fatḥa on the tāʾ for the passive, in pause, with the hamza joined, and iftaʿil for the command, confusion is required; so the tāʾ was given a ḍamma to remove it. Judge the rest by this.

parts.title: The participles and the nouns of time, place and instrument
parts.arabic: اسْمُ الْفَاعِلِ وَالْمَفْعُولِ وَالزَّمَانِ وَالْمَكَانِ وَالْآلَةِ

lessons.title: The active participle of the triliteral
body: The active participle “is a noun derived from the muḍāriʿ for the one in whom the act subsists, in the sense of occurring”: ḍārib is the one in whom hitting takes place, as an event, not as a lasting nature (that is the ṣifa mushabbaha of the next lesson). It is taken from the muḍāriʿ because the two correspond: both describe an indefinite noun, and more besides (lesson 15).

From the triliteral it is on the measure fāʿil. The book makes it from yaḍribu in two steps: “the sign of the future was dropped”, and “the alif was put between the fāʾ and the ʿayn”. Why there? “Because at the beginning it would resemble the speaker”: an alif before the root, aḍrib-, would look like aḍribu, “I hit”.

Its ʿayn has a kasra, and every other vowel is ruled out. A fatḥa would make it look like the past of the mufāʿala pattern: ḍāraba, “he fought with”. A ḍamma would be heavy. The kasra has its own problem, since it makes the participle look like the command of mufāʿala, ḍārib, “fight!”, but it was kept “out of necessity”. Others say this confusion is the best one to choose: the command comes from the future, and the participle resembles the future anyway.

So ḍārib is yaḍribu with its prefix traded for a long ā, and its pattern is the same for every bāb, whatever the vowel of the ʿayn in the future: nāṣir from yanṣuru, ʿālim from yaʿlamu, fātiḥ from yaftaḥu. Lesson 26 shows the book's reason for that sameness.

The trap the book itself points to: qātil, “killer”, the participle of qatala, and qātil, “fight!”, the command of qātala, are spelt and said alike. Context and the presence or absence of tanwīn tell them apart: qātilun is a noun, qātil without an ending is the command.

terms.en: the active participle: the one in whom the act takes place
the measure of the active participle of the triliteral
occurring: the act as an event, not a lasting quality
the pattern fāʿala yufāʿilu, whose past and command the participle resembles

tasks.prompt: Make ḍārib from yaḍribu as the book does, and say why the alif goes where it goes.
tasks.answer: Drop the prefix ya- (ḍribu), then put an alif between the fāʾ and the ʿayn: ḍārib. Not at the beginning, because an alif there would make it look like aḍribu, the speaker's form.

tasks.prompt: Why does the ʿayn of fāʿil have a kasra, and not a fatḥa or a ḍamma?
tasks.answer: With a fatḥa it would look like the past of mufāʿala (ḍāraba); with a ḍamma it would be heavy. The kasra makes it look like the command of mufāʿala, but it was kept out of necessity (or, others say, that confusion is the lightest, because the command and the participle both go back to the future).

tasks.prompt: Give the active participle of naṣara, ʿalima and ḥasiba with the conjugation tool.
tasks.answer: Nāṣir, ʿālim, ḥāsib (نَاصِرٌ، عَالِمٌ، حَاسِبٌ): the same measure fāʿil, whatever the vowel of the future.

quiz.prompt: The active participle is derived from…
quiz.explanation: Because they correspond in describing an indefinite and more.

quiz.prompt: Why was the alif not put at the start of ḍārib?
options: It would look like the speaker's aḍribu
It would be a hamza of joining
quiz.explanation: So it goes between the fāʾ and the ʿayn.

quiz.prompt: With a fatḥa on the ʿayn, fāʿil would look like…
quiz.explanation: Ḍāraba, “he fought with”.

quiz.prompt: With a kasra, fāʿil looks like…
quiz.explanation: Kept out of necessity.

quiz.prompt: The participle of naṣara is…
quiz.explanation: Fāʿil for every bāb; naṣīr is another pattern (lesson 25).

quiz.prompt: “In the sense of occurring” sets the participle apart from…
quiz.explanation: Ḍārib is one in whom hitting occurs.

quiz.prompt: The ḍamma on the ʿayn is rejected because it is…
quiz.explanation: “With a ḍamma it would be heavy.”

text.original: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنَ الْمُضَارِعِ لِمَنْ قَامَ بِهِ الْفِعْلُ بِمَعْنَى الْحُدُوثِ، وَاشْتُقَّ مِنْهُ لِمُنَاسَبَتِهِمَا فِي الْوُقُوعِ صِفَةً لِلنَّكِرَةِ وَغَيْرِهِ. وَصِيغَتُهُ مِنَ الثُّلَاثِيِّ عَلَى وَزْنِ فَاعِلٍ، وَحُذِفَ عَلَامَةُ الِاسْتِقْبَالِ مِنْ يَضْرِبُ، فَأُدْخِلَ الْأَلِفُ بَيْنَ الْفَاءِ وَالْعَيْنِ؛ لِأَنَّ فِي الْأَوَّلِ يَصِيرُ مُشَابِهًا لِلْمُتَكَلِّمِ.
text.en: It is a noun derived from the muḍāriʿ for the one in whom the act subsists, in the sense of occurring; it was derived from it because they correspond in coming as an adjective of an indefinite, and in other things. Its form from the triliteral is on the measure fāʿil: the sign of the future was dropped from yaḍribu, and the alif was put between the fāʾ and the ʿayn, because at the beginning it would resemble [the form of] the speaker.

text.original: وَكُسِرَ عَيْنُهُ؛ لِأَنَّ بِتَقْدِيرِ النَّصْبِ يَصِيرُ مُشَابِهًا بِمَاضِي الْمُفَاعَلَةِ، وَبِتَقْدِيرِ الضَّمِّ يَثْقُلُ، وَبِتَقْدِيرِ الْكَسْرِ أَيْضًا يَلْزَمُ الِالْتِبَاسُ بِأَمْرِ بَابِ الْمُفَاعَلَةِ، وَلَكِنْ أُبْقِيَ مَعَ ذَلِكَ لِلضَّرُورَةِ، وَقِيلَ: اخْتِيَارُ الِالْتِبَاسِ بِالْأَمْرِ أَوْلَى؛ لِأَنَّ الْأَمْرَ مِنَ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ، وَالْفَاعِلَ مُشَابِهٌ بِهِ.
text.en: Its ʿayn was given a kasra: with a fatḥa it would resemble the past of mufāʿala, and with a ḍamma it would be heavy; with a kasra too confusion with the command of the pattern mufāʿala is required, but it was kept despite that, out of necessity. It is also said: choosing confusion with the command is more fitting, because the command is from the future, and the fāʿil resembles it.

lessons.title: The adjective like the participle, and afʿal of preference
body: “The adjective like the participle” (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) describes a lasting quality, and it has many patterns: fariq, “fearful”; shakis, “ill-natured”; ṣulb, “hard”; milḥ, “salty”; junub, “in major impurity”; ḥasan, “good”; khashin, “rough”; jabān, “cowardly”; shujāʿ, “brave”; ʿaṭshān, “thirsty”; and aḥwal, “squint-eyed”, on afʿal.

That last pattern, afʿal for colours and defects, belongs to verbs on faʿila, “except six, which come from faʿula”: aḥmaq, “foolish”, akhraq, “clumsy”, ādam, “brown”, arʿan, “rash”, asmar, “dark”, aʿjaf, “lean”; al-Aṣmaʿī adds aʿjam, “speaking unclearly”. Al-Farrāʾ narrows the exceptions: aḥmaq comes from ḥamiqa, a dialect form of ḥamuqa, and khariqa, samira and ʿajifa likewise have faʿila beside faʿula.

Then afʿal of preference, “more, most”, “for the preference of the doer”. It comes only from a bare triliteral that is “neither a colour nor a defect”. Not from the augmented, because afʿal cannot keep all its letters: istakhraja has no room in afʿal. Not from colours and defects, because there afʿal is already the plain adjective, aḥmar, “red”, and a second afʿal meaning “redder” would be confused with it.

Nor is it used “for the preference of the object”. Why the doer and not the object? “The doer is intended, and the object is an extra in speech”; and every verb has a doer, while not every verb has an object, so only the doer allows a general rule. Three famous sayings break these rules and are called irregular: ashghalu min dhāti al-niḥyayni, “busier than the woman with the two butter-skins” (preference of the one busied); aʿṭāhum and awlāhum, “the most giving of them”, from augmented verbs; and aḥmaqu min Habannaqa, “more foolish than Habannaqa”, from a defect.

A beginner's trap: afʿal is three different things. Akrama is a verb (lesson 6), aḥmar is an adjective of colour, and akram, “nobler”, is a noun of preference. The pattern alone does not tell you which; the root and the sentence do.

terms.en: the adjective like the participle: a lasting quality
afʿal of preference: “more, most”
colour and defect, whose adjective is afʿal
an extra in speech: the object, which the sentence can do without
a Baṣran philologist and a Kūfan grammarian the book cites

examples.arabic: أَحْمَقَ، وَأَخْرَقَ، وَآدَمَ، وَأَرْعَنَ، وَأَسْمَرَ، وَأَعْجَفَ
examples.en: the six afʿal adjectives from faʿula
ashghalu min dhāti al-niḥyayni: preference of the object, irregular
aḥmaqu min Habannaqata: preference from a defect, irregular

tasks.prompt: Why can afʿal of preference not be made from istakhraja?
tasks.answer: Because it is augmented: afʿal has room for three root letters only, so it cannot keep all the letters of istakhraja. Afʿal of preference comes only from the bare triliteral.

tasks.prompt: Why is afʿal of preference not made from verbs of colour or defect?
tasks.answer: Because there afʿal is already the adjective (aḥmar, “red”; aḥwal, “squint-eyed”), and the preference would be confused with it.

tasks.prompt: Give the book's two reasons for making afʿal of preference for the doer, not the object.
tasks.answer: The doer is intended in speech and the object is an extra; and every verb has a doer, while not every verb has an object, so a general rule is possible only with the doer.

tasks.prompt: Why is each of these irregular: ashghalu min dhāti al-niḥyayni, aʿṭāhum, aḥmaqu min Habannaqa?
tasks.answer: Ashghalu is a preference of the one busied, the object; aʿṭāhum comes from the augmented aʿṭā; aḥmaqu comes from a defect, foolishness.

quiz.prompt: The ṣifa mushabbaha describes…
quiz.explanation: Ḥasan, shujāʿ, ʿaṭshān: qualities, not events.

quiz.prompt: The afʿal adjective of colour and defect belongs to verbs on…
quiz.explanation: Aḥmaq, akhraq, ādam, arʿan, asmar, aʿjaf come from faʿula.

quiz.prompt: Who added aʿjam to the six?
quiz.explanation: “Al-Aṣmaʿī added al-aʿjam.”

quiz.prompt: Afʿal of preference comes from…
options: a bare triliteral, not a colour or defect
quiz.explanation: The three conditions are given in the passage.

quiz.prompt: Why not afʿal of preference from aḥmar's verb?
options: It would be confused with the adjective aḥmar
quiz.explanation: In colours afʿal is already the adjective.

quiz.prompt: Ashghalu min dhāti al-niḥyayni is irregular because it is…
quiz.explanation: It means “more busied”.

quiz.prompt: Why is the object not given its own afʿal?
options: It is an extra, and not every verb has one
quiz.explanation: The doer is intended and general.

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ الصِّفَةُ الْمُشَبَّهَةُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْأَبْنِيَةِ، نَحْوُ: فَرِقٍ، وَشَكِسٍ، وَصُلْبٍ، وَمِلْحٍ، وَجُنُبٍ، وَحَسَنٍ، وَخَشِنٍ، وَجَبَانٍ، وَشُجَاعٍ، وَعَطْشَانَ، وَأَحْوَلَ، وَهُوَ مُخْتَصٌّ بِبَابِ فَعِلَ إِلَّا سِتَّةً؛ فَإِنَّهَا تَجِيءُ مِنْ فَعُلَ، نَحْوُ: أَحْمَقَ، وَأَخْرَقَ، وَآدَمَ، وَأَرْعَنَ، وَأَسْمَرَ، وَأَعْجَفَ، وَزَادَ الْأَصْمَعِيُّ: الْأَعْجَمَ. قَالَ الْفَرَّاءُ: أَحْمَقُ مِنْ حَمِقَ، وَهُوَ لُغَةٌ مِنْ حَمُقَ، وَكَذَلِكَ يَجِيءُ فِي خَرِقَ وَسَمِرَ وَعَجِفَ، أَعْنِي: فَعِلَ لُغَةٌ فِيهِنَّ.
text.en: The adjective like the participle (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) comes on these patterns, as fariqin “fearful”, shakisin “ill-natured”, ṣulbin “hard”, milḥin “salty”, junubin “in major impurity”, ḥasanin “good”, khashinin “rough”, jabānin “cowardly”, shujāʿin “brave”, ʿaṭshāna “thirsty” and aḥwala “squint-eyed”. It belongs to the pattern faʿila, except six, which come from faʿula: aḥmaqa “foolish”, akhraqa “clumsy”, ādama “brown”, arʿana “rash”, asmara “dark” and aʿjafa “lean”; and al-Aṣmaʿī added al-aʿjama “the one who speaks unclearly”. Al-Farrāʾ said: aḥmaq is from ḥamiqa, which is a dialect form of ḥamuqa; and likewise it comes in khariqa, samira and ʿajifa — I mean, faʿila is a dialect form in them.

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ أَفْعَلُ لِتَفْضِيلِ الْفَاعِلِ مِنَ الثُّلَاثِيِّ غَيْرِ مَزِيدٍ فِيهِ مِمَّا لَيْسَ بِلَوْنٍ وَلَا عَيْبٍ، وَلَا يَجِيءُ مِنَ الْمَزِيدِ فِيهِ لِعَدَمِ إِمْكَانِ مُحَافَظَةِ جَمِيعِ حُرُوفِهَا فِي أَفْعَلَ، وَلَا مِنْ لَوْنٍ وَلَا عَيْبٍ؛ لِأَنَّ فِيهِمَا يَجِيءُ أَفْعَلُ لِلصِّفَةِ، فَيَلْزَمُ الِالْتِبَاسُ.
text.en: Afʿal comes for the preference of the doer, from the triliteral that is not augmented, from what is neither a colour nor a defect. It does not come from the augmented, because keeping all its letters in afʿal is not possible; nor from a colour or a defect, because in them afʿal comes for the adjective, so confusion would be required.

text.original: وَلَا يَجِيءُ لِتَفْضِيلِ الْمَفْعُولِ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِتَفْضِيلِ الْفَاعِلِ، فَإِنْ قِيلَ: لِمَ لَا يُجْعَلُ عَلَى الْعَكْسِ حَتَّى لَا يَلْزَمَ الِالْتِبَاسُ؟ قُلْنَا: جَعْلُهُ لِلْفَاعِلِ أَوْلَى؛ لِأَنَّ الْفَاعِلَ مَقْصُودٌ، وَالْمَفْعُولَ فَضْلَةٌ فِي الْكَلَامِ، وَأَيْضًا يُمْكِنُ التَّعْمِيمُ فِي الْفَاعِلِ دُونَ الْمَفْعُولِ. وَنَحْوُ: أَشْغَلُ مِنْ ذَاتِ النِّحْيَيْنِ لِتَفْضِيلِ الْمَفْعُولِ، وَهُوَ أَعْطَاهُمْ وَأَوْلَاهُمْ مِنَ الزَّوَائِدِ، وَأَحْمَقُ مِنْ هَبَنَّقَةَ مِنَ الْعُيُوبِ، شَاذٌّ.
text.en: It does not come for the preference of the object, so that it is not confused with the preference of the doer. If it is said: why is it not made the other way round, so that confusion is not required? we say: making it for the doer is more fitting, because the doer is intended and the object is an extra in speech; also, generalising is possible in the doer and not in the object. The like of ashghalu min dhāti al-niḥyayni “busier than the woman with the two butter-skins”, for the preference of the object; aʿṭāhum “the most giving of them” and awlāhum “the most bestowing of them”, from the augmented; and aḥmaqu min Habannaqata “more foolish than Habannaqa”, from the defects, is irregular.

lessons.title: Faʿīl, faʿūl and the patterns of intensity
body: The doer also comes on faʿīl: naṣīr, “helper”. But faʿīl often means the one done to: qatīl, “killed”, jarīḥ, “wounded”. When it does, “the masculine and the feminine are the same”: a woman is qatīl, without a tāʾ, “to distinguish the doer from the object”. Once such a word becomes a plain noun it takes the tāʾ: dhabīḥa, “an animal for slaughter”, laqīṭa, “a foundling”. And a faʿīl of the doer is sometimes treated the same way, as in inna raḥmata Allāhi qarībun mina al-muḥsinīna (7:56), with qarīb for the feminine raḥma.

Faʿūl comes for intensity, manūʿ, “much withholding”, and here the rule turns round: when faʿūl means the doer, masculine and feminine are the same, imraʾatun ṣabūrun, “a patient woman”; when it means the object, it takes the tāʾ, nāqatun ḥalūbatun, “a milch camel”, the camel that is milked. “Sameness was given in faʿīl to the object and in faʿūl to the doer, seeking balance.”

More patterns of intensity follow: ṣabbār, “very patient”; mijdham, “a cutting sword”, which is also a pattern of the instrument; fissīq, “very sinful”; kubbār, ṭuwwāl, “very big, very tall”; ʿallāma, nassāba, rāwiya, “very learned, a great genealogist, a great transmitter”; farūqa, ḍuḥaka, mijdhāma, misqām, miʿṭīr. In the last nine masculine and feminine are the same, “because they are few”: a man is ʿallāma, with the tāʾ, which here marks intensity, not the feminine.

Two apparent breaks of the rule are explained by analogy (ḥaml). Miskīna, “a poor woman”, takes the tāʾ though mifʿīl should not, because it is treated like faqīra. And hiya ʿaduwwatu Allāhi, “she is the enemy of God”, has the tāʾ though faʿūl of the doer should not, because it is treated like ṣadīqa, “friend”, its opposite.
Put simply: a tāʾ at the end of an adjective does not always mean “feminine”. In ʿallāma it means “very”; and its absence in qatīl or ṣabūr does not mean “masculine”.

terms.en: faʿīl meaning the one done to: qatīl, jarīḥ
a pattern of intensity: ṣabūr, manūʿ
the patterns of intensity: ṣabbār, fissīq, ʿallāma
treating a word like another, by analogy

examples.en: qatīl, jarīḥ: faʿīl of the object, the same for a woman
imraʾatun ṣabūrun: faʿūl of the doer, without the tāʾ
nāqatun ḥalūbatun: faʿūl of the object, with the tāʾ
ʿallāma, nassāba, rāwiya: the tāʾ of intensity, said of men
hiya ʿaduwwatu Allāhi: the tāʾ by analogy with ṣadīqa

tasks.prompt: Why is a woman called qatīl, without a tāʾ, but an animal for slaughter dhabīḥa?
tasks.answer: Faʿīl in the sense of the object is the same for both genders, to tell it from faʿīl of the doer. Dhabīḥa has become a noun, one of the names of things, and then it takes the tāʾ.

tasks.prompt: Explain the “balance” between faʿīl and faʿūl.
tasks.answer: In faʿīl the sameness of genders goes to the object (qatīl), in faʿūl to the doer (ṣabūr); the object of faʿūl and the doer of faʿīl take the tāʾ. Each pattern gives the sameness to one side.

tasks.prompt: Why do the Arabs say rajulun ʿallāmatun of a man?
tasks.answer: The tāʾ of ʿallāma is a mark of intensity, not of the feminine; in these rare patterns masculine and feminine are the same.

tasks.prompt: How does the book explain the tāʾ in miskīna and in ʿaduwwatu Allāhi?
tasks.answer: By analogy: miskīna is treated like faqīra, “poor (f.)”, and ʿaduwwa like ṣadīqa, “friend (f.)”, which take the tāʾ.

quiz.prompt: Qatīl, “killed”, used of a woman, is…
quiz.explanation: Faʿīl of the object is the same for both.

quiz.prompt: Dhabīḥa takes the tāʾ because it…
quiz.explanation: It is counted among the nouns.

quiz.prompt: Imraʾatun ṣabūrun shows that faʿūl of the doer…
options: is the same for both genders
quiz.explanation: Ṣabūr without a tāʾ for a woman.

quiz.prompt: Nāqatun ḥalūbatun has the tāʾ because ḥalūba means…
quiz.explanation: Faʿūl of the object takes the tāʾ.

quiz.prompt: In ʿallāma, said of a man, the tāʾ marks…
quiz.explanation: In the last nine patterns the genders are the same.

quiz.prompt: Mijdham is shared between…
quiz.explanation: Sayfun mijdham: a sword that cuts much.

quiz.prompt: ʿAduwwatu Allāhi takes the tāʾ by analogy with…
quiz.explanation: Its opposite, the woman friend.

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ الْفَاعِلُ عَلَى وَزْنِ فَعِيلٍ، نَحْوُ: نَصِيرٍ، وَيَسْتَوِي فِيهِ الْمُذَكَّرُ وَالْمُؤَنَّثُ إِذَا كَانَ بِمَعْنَى الْمَفْعُولِ، نَحْوُ: قَتِيلٍ وَجَرِيحٍ؛ فَرْقًا بَيْنَ الْفَاعِلِ وَالْمَفْعُولِ، إِلَّا إِذَا جُعِلَتِ الْكَلِمَةُ مِنْ عِدَادِ الْأَسْمَاءِ، نَحْوُ: ذَبِيحَةٍ وَلَقِيطَةٍ، وَقَدْ يُشَبَّهُ بِهِ مَا هُوَ بِمَعْنَى الْفَاعِلِ، نَحْوُ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ رَحْمَةَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
text.en: The doer comes on the measure faʿīl, as naṣīrin “helper”. The masculine and the feminine are the same in it when it is in the sense of the object, as qatīlin “killed” and jarīḥin “wounded”, to distinguish the doer from the object — except when the word is made one of the nouns, as dhabīḥatin “slaughtered animal” and laqīṭatin “foundling”. What is in the sense of the doer is sometimes likened to it, as His saying, Most High: inna raḥmata Allāhi qarībun mina al-muḥsinīna “the mercy of God is near to those who do good” [7:56].

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ فَعُولٌ لِلْمُبَالَغَةِ، نَحْوُ: مَنُوعٍ، وَيَسْتَوِي فِيهِ الْمُذَكَّرُ وَالْمُؤَنَّثُ إِذَا كَانَ بِمَعْنَى فَاعِلٍ، نَحْوُ: امْرَأَةٌ صَبُورٌ، وَيُقَالُ فِي الْمَفْعُولِ: نَاقَةٌ حَلُوبَةٌ، وَأُعْطِيَ الِاسْتِوَاءُ فِي فَعِيلٍ لِلْمَفْعُولِ، وَفِي فَعُولٍ لِلْفَاعِلِ؛ طَلَبًا لِلْعَدْلِ.
text.en: Faʿūl comes for intensiveness, as manūʿin “much withholding”. The masculine and the feminine are the same in it when it is in the sense of fāʿil, as imraʾatun ṣabūrun “a patient woman”; and for the object one says nāqatun ḥalūbatun “a milch camel”. Sameness was given in faʿīl to the object and in faʿūl to the doer, seeking balance.

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ لِلْمُبَالَغَةِ، نَحْوُ: صَبَّارٍ، وَسَيْفٍ مِجْذَمٍ، وَهُوَ مُشْتَرَكٌ بَيْنَ الْآلَةِ وَبَيْنَ الْمُبَالَغَةِ لِلْفَاعِلِ، وَفِسِّيقٍ، وَكُبَّارٍ، وَطُوَّالٍ، وَعَلَّامَةٍ، وَنَسَّابَةٍ، وَرَاوِيَةٍ، وَفَرُوقَةٍ، وَضُحَكَةٍ، وَمِجْذَامَةٍ، وَمِسْقَامٍ، وَمِعْطِيرٍ، وَيَسْتَوِي الْمُذَكَّرُ وَالْمُؤَنَّثُ فِي التِّسْعَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ لِقِلَّتِهِنَّ. وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُمْ: مِسْكِينَةٌ، فَمَحْمُولَةٌ عَلَى فَقِيرَةٍ، كَمَا قَالُوا: هِيَ عَدُوَّةُ اللَّهِ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَدْخُلِ الْهَاءُ فِي فَعُولٍ الَّذِي لِلْفَاعِلِ، حَمْلًا عَلَى صَدِيقَةٍ.
text.en: It also comes for intensiveness [on other patterns], as ṣabbārin “very patient”; sayfin mijdhamin “a cutting sword”, which is shared between the instrument and intensiveness for the doer; fissīqin “very sinful”, kubbārin “very big”, ṭuwwālin “very tall”, ʿallāmatin “very learned”, nassābatin “great genealogist”, rāwiyatin “great transmitter”, farūqatin “very fearful”, ḍuḥakatin “much laughing”, mijdhāmatin “very decisive”, misqāmin “often ill” and miʿṭīrin “much perfumed”. The masculine and the feminine are the same in the last nine because they are few. As for their saying miskīnatun “poor (f.)”, it is treated like faqīratin “poor (f.)”; as they said hiya ʿaduwwatu Allāhi “she is the enemy of God”, though the hāʾ does not enter the faʿūl that is for the doer, treating it like ṣadīqatin “friend (f.)”.

lessons.title: The participles of the longer verbs, and the passive participle
lessons.arabic: اسْمُ الْفَاعِلِ مِنْ غَيْرِ الثُّلَاثِيِّ وَاسْمُ الْمَفْعُولِ
lessons.transliteration: ism al-fāʿil min ghayr al-thulāthī wa-ism al-mafʿūl
body: From verbs longer than three letters the active participle is “on the form of the future, with a mīm with ḍamma and a kasra on what is before the last”: yukrimu gives mukrim. A mīm, because a weak letter cannot stand there, and the mīm is near the wāw, both made with the lips; with a ḍamma, to tell it from the noun of place, which has mafʿal. Musʹhab, with a fatḥa, as the doer of asʹhaba, “to speak at length”, and yāfiʿ, “a youth”, from ayfaʿa, are irregular. In ḍāriba, “hitting (f.)”, the letter before the tāʾ is fixed on a fatḥa, because the tāʾ has made it “the middle of the word”.

The passive participle “is a noun derived from yufʿalu for the one on whom the act falls”, on the measure mafʿūl: maḍrūb. The book builds it from yuḍrabu in four steps. The mīm takes the place of the prefix, as in the active: muḍrab. The mīm takes a fatḥa, so as not to look like the passive participle of afʿala (mukram): maḍrab. The rāʾ takes a ḍamma, so as not to look like the noun of place: maḍrub. Then the ḍamma is drawn out, “because mafʿul without the tāʾ does not exist in their speech”: maḍrūb.

Why was the triliteral's mafʿūl changed so much, when the passive participle of the other verbs (mustakhraj) and the noun of place keep the shape of their future? “So that it resembles the active participle in being changed”: the fāʿil too was changed, for by rule it should have been fāʿal from yafʿalu and fāʿul from yafʿulu, and it is fāʿil for every bāb. The two participles were changed together “for brotherhood between them”.
From the longer verbs the passive participle is the active one “with a fatḥa on what is before the last”: mustakhrij, mustakhraj; mukrim, mukram. One letter tells the doer from the one done to.
The conjugation tool gives both participles of every sound pattern; check the rule against it: the kasra or the fatḥa before the last letter is the whole difference.

terms.en: the passive participle: the one on whom the act falls
its measure from the triliteral
the mīm with ḍamma of the longer verbs' participles
brotherhood: the two participles changed alike

examples.en: mukrim, mukram: the active and passive participles of akrama (conjugation tool)
musʹhab and yāfiʿ: irregular participles
mustakhrij, mustakhraj: a kasra or a fatḥa before the last (conjugation tool)

tasks.prompt: Build maḍrūb from yuḍrabu in the book's four steps.
tasks.answer: Put a mīm for the prefix: muḍrab. Give the mīm a fatḥa, not to look like mukram: maḍrab. Give the rāʾ a ḍamma, not to look like the noun of place: maḍrub. Draw out the ḍamma, since mafʿul without tāʾ does not exist: maḍrūb.

tasks.prompt: Give both participles of akrama and istakhraja with the conjugation tool, and state the rule.
tasks.answer: Mukrim, mukram; mustakhrij, mustakhraj. The future's form with a mīm with ḍamma; a kasra before the last letter for the active, a fatḥa for the passive.

tasks.prompt: Why was the triliteral's passive participle changed, by the book's reason?
tasks.answer: To match the active participle, which was also changed: by rule it should have been fāʿal or fāʿul after the future, and it is fāʿil everywhere. The two were changed together for brotherhood.

quiz.prompt: The active participle of the longer verbs begins with…
quiz.explanation: Mukrim, mustakhrij.

quiz.prompt: Why a ḍamma on that mīm?
options: To tell it from the noun of place
quiz.explanation: The place has mafʿal.

quiz.prompt: Mukrim and mukram differ in…
options: the vowel before the last letter
quiz.explanation: Kasra for the doer, fatḥa for the one done to.

quiz.prompt: The passive participle is derived from…
quiz.explanation: From the passive future: yuḍrabu.

quiz.prompt: In building maḍrūb, why does the mīm take a fatḥa?
options: Not to look like the place
Not to look like the participle of afʿala
quiz.explanation: Muḍrab would look like mukram.

quiz.prompt: Why is the ḍamma of maḍrub drawn out?
options: Mafʿul without the tāʾ does not exist
quiz.explanation: Hence maḍrūb.

quiz.prompt: Which participle is irregular?
quiz.explanation: It is made as if from the bare verb.

text.original: وَصِيغَتُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ الثُّلَاثِيِّ عَلَى صِيغَةِ الْمُسْتَقْبَلِ بِمِيمٍ مَضْمُومَةٍ، وَكَسْرِ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ، نَحْوُ: مُكْرِمٍ، فَاخْتِيرَ الْمِيمُ لِتَعَذُّرِ حَرْفِ الْعِلَّةِ، وَقُرْبِ الْمِيمِ مِنَ الْوَاوِ فِي كَوْنِهَا شَفَوِيَّةً، وَضُمَّ الْمِيمُ لِلْفَرْقِ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْمَوْضِعِ، وَنَحْوُ: مُسْهَبٍ لِلْفَاعِلِ مِنْ أَسْهَبَ، وَيَافِعٍ مِنْ أَيْفَعَ، شَاذٌّ. وَيُبْنَى مَا قَبْلَ تَاءِ التَّأْنِيثِ عَلَى الْحَرَكَةِ فِي نَحْوِ: ضَارِبَةٍ؛ لِأَنَّهُ صَارَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ وَسَطِ الْكَلِمَةِ، كَمَا فِي نُونِ التَّأْكِيدِ وَيَاءِ النِّسْبَةِ، وَعَلَى الْفَتْحِ لِلْخِفَّةِ.
text.en: Its form from the non-triliteral is on the form of the future, with a mīm with ḍamma and a kasra on what is before the last, as mukrimin “honouring”. The mīm was chosen because a letter of weakness is not possible, and because the mīm is near the wāw in being a letter of the lips; and the mīm was given a ḍamma to distinguish it from the place. The like of musʹhabin for the doer from asʹhaba “he spoke at length”, and yāfiʿin “youth” from ayfaʿa “he grew up”, is irregular. What is before the tāʾ of the feminine is made mabnī on a vowel in the like of ḍāribatin “hitting (f.)”, because it has come to stand as the middle of the word, as with the nūn of emphasis and the yāʾ of relation; and on the fatḥa, for lightness.

text.original: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْ يُفْعَلُ لِمَنْ وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِعْلُ، وَصِيغَتُهُ مِنَ الثُّلَاثِيِّ عَلَى وَزْنِ مَفْعُولٍ، نَحْوُ: مَضْرُوبٍ.
text.en: It is a noun derived from yufʿalu for the one on whom the act falls; its form from the triliteral is on the measure mafʿūl, as maḍrūbin “hit”.

text.original: وَهُوَ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْ يُضْرَبُ لِمُنَاسَبَةٍ بَيْنَهُمَا، فَأُدْخِلَ الْمِيمُ مَقَامَ الزَّائِدِ لِتَعَذُّرِ حَرْفِ الْعِلَّةِ، فَصَارَ مُضْرَبٌ، ثُمَّ فُتِحَ الْمِيمُ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِمَفْعُولِ بَابِ الْإِفْعَالِ، فَصَارَ مَضْرَبٌ، ثُمَّ ضُمَّ الرَّاءُ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِالْمَوْضِعِ، فَصَارَ مَضْرُبٌ، ثُمَّ أُشْبِعَ الضَّمَّةُ لِانْعِدَامِ مَفْعُلٍ فِي كَلَامِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ التَّاءِ، فَصَارَ مَضْرُوبٌ.
text.en: It is derived from yuḍrabu because of a correspondence between them: the mīm was put in the place of the added [letter], because a letter of weakness is not possible, so it became muḍrabun; then the mīm was given a fatḥa so that it is not confused with the mafʿūl of the pattern ifʿāl, so it became maḍrabun; then the rāʾ was given a ḍamma so that it is not confused with the place, so it became maḍrubun; then the ḍamma was lengthened, because mafʿul without the tāʾ does not exist in their speech, so it became maḍrūbun.

text.original: وَغُيِّرَ مَفْعُولُ الثُّلَاثِيِّ دُونَ مَفْعُولِ سَائِرِ الْأَفْعَالِ وَالْمَوْضِعِ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ مُشَابِهًا فِي التَّغْيِيرِ بِاسْمِ الْفَاعِلِ، أَعْنِي: غُيِّرَ الْفَاعِلُ مِنْ يَفْعَلُ وَمِنْ يَفْعُلُ إِلَى فَاعِلٍ، وَالْقِيَاسُ فَاعَلٌ وَفَاعُلٌ، فَغُيِّرَ الْمَفْعُولُ أَيْضًا لِمُؤَاخَاةٍ بَيْنَهُمَا. وَصِيغَتُهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ الثُّلَاثِيِّ عَلَى صِيغَةِ الْفَاعِلِ بِفَتْحِ مَا قَبْلَ الْآخِرِ، نَحْوُ: مُسْتَخْرَجٍ.
text.en: The mafʿūl of the triliteral was changed, and not the mafʿūl of the other verbs nor the place, so that it resembles the active participle in being changed: I mean, the fāʿil was changed from yafʿalu and from yafʿulu to fāʿil, while the rule is fāʿal and fāʿul; so the mafʿūl was changed too, for brotherhood between them. Its form from the non-triliteral is on the form of the fāʿil with a fatḥa on what is before the last, as mustakhrajin “drawn out”.

lessons.title: The nouns of time, place and instrument
body: The noun of place is “derived from yafʿalu for the place in which the act occurs”. It takes a mīm, as the passive participle does, but no wāw, “so that it is not confused with it”. From a future with fatḥa it is mafʿal: madhhab, “the place of going”. From the mithāl it is mafʿil even with fatḥa: mawjil, “the place of fear”, from wajila yawjalu, because mawjal could be taken for fawʿal, like jawrab, “sock”; with a kasra no one thinks of fawʿil, a pattern that does not exist.

From a future with kasra it is mafʿil, except from the defective, which takes mafʿal, as marmā, “the place of throwing”, from yarmī, “fleeing from a succession of kasras”. From a future with ḍamma mafʿul is never made, “because of the heaviness of the ḍamma”; its place is shared: eleven nouns take mafʿil (mansik, majzir, manbit, maṭliʿ, mashriq, maghrib, mafriq, masqiṭ, maskin, marfiq, masjid) and the rest mafʿal, for its lightness. So masjid, from sajada yasjudu, has a kasra by exception.

“The noun of time is like the noun of place”: one form serves both, and the sentence tells which. Maqtal al-Ḥusayn, from qatala yaqtulu, can be “the place where al-Ḥusayn was killed” or “the time of his killing”.

The noun of instrument is mifʿal, with a kasra on the mīm “to distinguish it from the place”, and the morphologists' saying sums up the four patterns: “mafʿal for the place, mifʿal for the instrument, faʿla for the single time, fiʿla for the manner”. It also comes on mifʿāl: miqrāḍ, “scissors”, miftāḥ, “key”.

Some words look like instruments with a ḍamma on mīm and ʿayn: musʿuṭ, “snuff-box”, munkhul, “sieve”, mudhun, “oil-flask”, muduqq, “pestle”. Sībawayh says they are not instruments in the strict sense but “counted among the nouns”: names of these vessels, learnt one by one, not made by the rule.

terms.en: the noun of place: mafʿal or mafʿil
the noun of time: the same forms as the noun of place
the noun of instrument: mifʿal, mifʿāl
the patterns of the single time and of the manner

examples.en: al-madhhab, al-mawjil: mafʿal, and mafʿil from the mithāl
al-marmā: mafʿal from the defective, against a run of kasras
maqtal al-Ḥusayn: place or time of the killing
miqrāḍ, miftāḥ: instruments on mifʿāl

tasks.prompt: Why is the noun of place from wajila yawjalu mawjil, with a kasra, though the future has a fatḥa?
tasks.answer: With a fatḥa, mawjal could be taken for the pattern fawʿal, like jawrab, a plain noun. With a kasra there is no such danger, because fawʿil does not exist in Arabic.

tasks.prompt: Why marmā and not marmī from yarmī?
tasks.answer: The rule for a future with kasra is mafʿil, but the defective takes mafʿal to flee from a succession of kasras (a kasra on the ʿayn, then the yāʾ and the kasra of the ending).

tasks.prompt: Why does masjid have a kasra, though sajada yasjudu has a ḍamma in the future?
tasks.answer: Mafʿul is never made from yafʿulu; its place is divided between mafʿal and mafʿil, and masjid is one of the eleven nouns given mafʿil. The rest, like maqtal, take mafʿal.

tasks.prompt: Give the four patterns of the saying of the morphologists.
tasks.answer: Mafʿal for the place, mifʿal for the instrument, faʿla for the single time, fiʿla for the manner.

quiz.prompt: Why does the noun of place have no wāw?
options: Not to be confused with the passive participle
quiz.explanation: Mafʿūl has the wāw.

quiz.prompt: From yafʿalu the noun of place is…
quiz.explanation: Madhhab, from dhahaba yadhhabu.

quiz.prompt: Mawjil has a kasra so that it is not taken for…
quiz.explanation: Like jawrab; fawʿil does not exist.

quiz.prompt: From the defective the noun of place is…
quiz.explanation: To flee from a run of kasras.

quiz.prompt: Masjid has a kasra because it is…
options: one of the eleven exceptions from yafʿulu
quiz.explanation: The rest from yafʿulu take mafʿal.

quiz.prompt: The noun of instrument is…
quiz.explanation: With kasra on the mīm, to tell it from the place.

quiz.prompt: For Sībawayh, al-munkhul, “sieve”, is…
options: a name of a vessel, not an instrument by rule
quiz.explanation: “These two are counted among the nouns.”

text.original: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْ يَفْعَلُ لِمَكَانٍ وَقَعَ فِيهِ الْفِعْلُ، فَزِيدَتِ الْمِيمُ كَمَا فِي الْمَفْعُولِ لِمُنَاسَبَةٍ بَيْنَهُمَا، وَلَمْ يُزَدِ الْوَاوُ حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِهِ. وَصِيغَتُهُ مِنْ يَفْعَلُ مَفْعَلٌ كَالْمَذْهَبِ، إِلَّا مِنَ الْمِثَالِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ بِكَسْرِ الْعَيْنِ فِيهِ، نَحْوُ: الْمَوْجِلِ، حَتَّى لَا يُظَنَّ أَنَّ وَزْنَهُ فَوْعَلٌ مِثْلُ جَوْرَبٍ؛ لِأَنَّهُ اسْمٌ لَيْسَ مِنِ اسْمِ الْمَكَانِ وَالزَّمَانِ، وَلَا يُظَنُّ فِي الْكَسْرِ فَوْعَلًا؛ لِأَنَّ فَوْعِلًا بِكَسْرِ الْعَيْنِ لَا يُوجَدُ فِي كَلَامِهِمْ.
text.en: It is a noun derived from yafʿalu for the place in which the act occurs. The mīm was added as in the mafʿūl, because of a correspondence between them, and the wāw was not added, so that it is not confused with it. Its form from yafʿalu is mafʿal, as al-madhhabi “the place of going” — except from the mithāl, for there it has a kasra on the ʿayn, as al-mawjili “the place of fear”, so that it is not thought that its measure is fawʿal, like jawrabin “sock”, which is a noun that is not a noun of place or time; and with the kasra fawʿal is not thought of, because fawʿil, with a kasra on the ʿayn, is not found in their speech.

text.original: وَمِنْ يَفْعِلُ مَفْعِلٌ، إِلَّا مِنَ النَّاقِصِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ بِفَتْحِ الْعَيْنِ فِيهِ، نَحْوُ: الْمَرْمَى؛ فِرَارًا عَنْ تَوَالِي الْكَسَرَاتِ. وَلَا يُبْنَى مِنْ يَفْعُلُ مَفْعُلٌ لِثِقَلِ الضَّمَّةِ، فَقُسِمَ مَوْضِعُهُ بَيْنَ مَفْعَلٍ وَمَفْعِلٍ، وَأُعْطِيَ لِلْمَفْعِلِ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ اسْمًا، نَحْوُ: الْمَنْسِكِ، وَالْمَجْزِرِ، وَالْمَنْبِتِ، وَالْمَطْلِعِ، وَالْمَشْرِقِ، وَالْمَغْرِبِ، وَالْمَفْرِقِ، وَالْمَسْقِطِ، وَالْمَسْكِنِ، وَالْمَرْفِقِ، وَالْمَسْجِدِ، وَالْبَاقِي لِلْمَفْعَلِ لِخِفَّةِ الْفَتْحَةِ. وَاسْمُ الزَّمَانِ مِثْلُ الْمَكَانِ، نَحْوُ: مَقْتَلِ الْحُسَيْنِ.
text.en: From yafʿilu [it is] mafʿil — except from the defective, for there it has a fatḥa on the ʿayn, as al-marmā “the place of throwing”, fleeing from a succession of kasras. Mafʿul is not built from yafʿulu, because of the heaviness of the ḍamma; so its place was divided between mafʿal and mafʿil: mafʿil was given eleven nouns, as al-mansiki “the place of sacrifice”, al-majziri “the slaughter-place”, al-manbiti “the place of growth”, al-maṭliʿi “the place of rising”, al-mashriqi “the east”, al-maghribi “the west”, al-mafriqi “the parting of the hair”, al-masqiṭi “the place of falling”, al-maskini “the dwelling”, al-marfiqi “the elbow” and al-masjidi “the mosque”; and the rest [went] to mafʿal, because of the lightness of the fatḥa. The noun of time is like the noun of place, as maqtali al-Ḥusayni “the time of the killing of al-Ḥusayn”.

text.original: وَهُوَ اسْمٌ مُشْتَقٌّ مِنْ يَفْعَلُ لِلْآلَةِ، وَصِيغَتُهُ مِفْعَلٌ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ قَالَ الصَّرْفِيُّونَ: الْمَفْعَلُ لِلْمَوْضِعِ، وَالْمِفْعَلُ لِلْآلَةِ، وَالْفَعْلَةُ لِلْمَرَّةِ، وَالْفِعْلَةُ لِلْحَالَةِ، وَكُسِرَتِ الْمِيمُ لِلْفَرْقِ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْمَوْضِعِ.
text.en: It is a noun derived from yafʿalu for the instrument, and its form is mifʿal. For this reason the morphologists said: mafʿal is for the place, mifʿal for the instrument, faʿla for the single time and fiʿla for the manner; and the mīm was given a kasra to distinguish it from the place.

text.original: وَيَجِيءُ عَلَى وَزْنِ مِفْعَالٍ، نَحْوُ: مِقْرَاضٍ وَمِفْتَاحٍ، وَيَجِيءُ مَضْمُومَ الْمِيمِ وَالْعَيْنِ، نَحْوُ: الْمُسْعُطِ وَالْمُنْخُلِ. قَالَ سِيبَوَيْهِ: هَذَانِ مِنْ عِدَادِ الْأَسْمَاءِ، يَعْنِي: الْمُسْعُطُ وَالْمُنْخُلُ اسْمٌ لِهَذَا الْوِعَاءِ، وَلَيْسَ بِآلَةٍ، وَكَذَلِكَ أَخَوَاتُهُ: الْمُدْهُنُ وَالْمُدُقُّ.
text.en: It comes on the measure mifʿāl, as miqrāḍin “scissors” and miftāḥin “key”; and it comes with a ḍamma on the mīm and the ʿayn, as al-musʿuṭi “snuff-box” and al-munkhuli “sieve”. Sībawayh said: these two are counted among the nouns; that is, al-musʿuṭ and al-munkhul are names of these vessels, not instruments; and likewise their sisters al-mudʹhunu “oil-flask” and al-muduqqu “pestle”.

lessons.title: The doubled verb, and what idghām is
body: The second chapter takes the doubled verb, whose ʿayn and lām are the same letter: madda, “to stretch”, from m-d-d. It is also called aṣamm, “deaf”, “because of its hardness”: the doubled letter is pressed hard. It is not called sound, though it has no weak letter, because one of its two like letters can turn into a weak letter: taqaḍḍā al-bāzī, “the falcon swooped down”, is from taqaḍḍaḍa, whose last ḍād has become an alif.

It comes from three bābs: sarra yasurru, “to gladden”; farra yafirru, “to flee”; and ʿaḍḍa yaʿaḍḍu, “to bite”, which is ʿaḍiḍa underneath, the bāb of ʿalima. From faʿula yafʿulu it comes only rarely: ḥabba fa-huwa ḥabībun, labba fa-huwa labībun, “he became beloved, so he is beloved; he became wise, so he is wise”, where the adjective faʿīl shows the bāb of faʿula.

The chapter's tool is idghām, assimilation: “when two letters of one kind come together, or two letters close in their point of articulation, the first is assimilated into the second, because of the heaviness of what is repeated”. Madda shows two of one kind, d and d; akhraja shaṭʾahu (48:29), as some readers recite it, shows two close letters, the jīm and the shīn, across two words.

What is idghām, exactly? One group, following “the great scholar Jār Allāh”, al-Zamakhsharī, says: “holding the letter in its point of articulation for as long as two letters are held”, a single long sound. Others: “making the first unvowelled and folding it into the second”. The first describes what the ear hears; the second, the steps by which the form is built, and it is the one the book uses.

In writing, the merged letters are “two letters in pronunciation and one in writing”, as madda with its shadda; or “two in pronunciation and in writing”, as al-raḥmān, where the lām of the article is written but said as a second rāʾ.

terms.en: the doubled verb: its ʿayn and lām alike
“the deaf”: another name of the doubled verb
assimilation: the first letter folded into the second
two letters of one kind, and two close in articulation
al-Zamakhsharī, author of the Mufaṣṣal and the Kashshāf

examples.en: taqaḍḍā al-bāzī: a doubled letter turned weak
ḥabba fa-huwa ḥabībun: the rare bāb of faʿula
akhraja shaṭʾahu: two close letters, jīm and shīn
al-raḥmān: merged, yet both letters written

tasks.prompt: Why is madda not called sound, though it has no weak letter?
tasks.answer: Because in the doubled verb one of the two like letters can become a weak letter, as in taqaḍḍā al-bāzī, from taqaḍḍaḍa, whose last ḍād became an alif.

tasks.prompt: Give the three bābs of the doubled verb with the book's examples.
tasks.answer: Sarra yasurru (a–u), farra yafirru (a–i), ʿaḍḍa yaʿaḍḍu (i–a); and rarely faʿula yafʿulu, as ḥabba fa-huwa ḥabīb.

tasks.prompt: State the two definitions of idghām and say which the book's analyses use.
tasks.answer: Holding the letter in its point of articulation as long as two letters are held (reported from al-Zamakhsharī); and making the first quiescent and folding it into the second. The analyses use the second: first a sukūn, then the folding.

quiz.prompt: The doubled verb is also called…
quiz.explanation: Because of its hardness.

quiz.explanation: As in taqaḍḍā al-bāzī.

quiz.explanation: Sarra yasurru, farra yafirru, ʿaḍḍa yaʿaḍḍu.

quiz.prompt: ʿAḍḍa yaʿaḍḍu belongs to the bāb of…
quiz.explanation: It is ʿaḍiḍa yaʿaḍḍu, i–a.

quiz.explanation: Li-thiqal al-mukarrar.

quiz.explanation: The jīm and the shīn.

text.original: وَيُقَالُ لَهُ: أَصَمُّ؛ لِشِدَّتِهِ، وَلَا يُقَالُ لَهُ: صَحِيحٌ؛ لِصَيْرُورَةِ أَحَدِ حَرْفَيْهِ حَرْفَ عِلَّةٍ فِي نَحْوِ: تَقَضَّى الْبَازِي. وَهُوَ يَجِيءُ مِنْ ثَلَاثَةِ أَبْوَابٍ، نَحْوُ: سَرَّ يَسُرُّ، وَفَرَّ يَفِرُّ، وَعَضَّ يَعَضُّ، وَلَا يَجِيءُ مِنْ بَابِ فَعُلَ يَفْعُلُ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا، نَحْوُ: حَبَّ فَهُوَ حَبِيبٌ، وَلَبَّ فَهُوَ لَبِيبٌ.
text.en: It is called aṣammu “deaf” because of its hardness; and it is not called ṣaḥīḥ “sound”, because one of its two [like] letters becomes a letter of weakness in the like of taqaḍḍā al-bāzī “the falcon swooped down”. It comes from three bābs, as sarra yasurru “to gladden”, farra yafirru “to flee” and ʿaḍḍa yaʿaḍḍu “to bite”; and it does not come from the bāb of faʿula yafʿulu except rarely, as ḥabba fa-huwa ḥabībun “he became beloved, so he is beloved” and labba fa-huwa labībun “he became wise, so he is wise”.

text.original: وَإِذَا اجْتَمَعَ حَرْفَانِ مِنْ جِنْسٍ وَاحِدٍ، أَوْ حَرْفَانِ مُتَقَارِبَانِ فِي الْمَخْرَجِ، يُدْغَمُ الْأَوَّلُ فِي الثَّانِي لِثِقَلِ الْمُكَرَّرِ، نَحْوُ: مَدَّ، وَنَحْوُ: ﴿أَخْرَجَ شَطْأَهُ﴾. وَقَالَتْ طَائِفَةٌ: الْإِدْغَامُ إِلْبَاثُ الْحَرْفِ فِي مَخْرَجِهِ مِقْدَارَ إِلْبَاثِ الْحَرْفَيْنِ، كَذَا نُقِلَ عَنْ جَارِ اللَّهِ الْعَلَّامَةِ. وَقِيلَ: إِسْكَانُ الْأَوَّلِ وَإِدْرَاجُهُ فِي الثَّانِي. وَالْمُدْغَمُ فِيهِ حَرْفَانِ فِي اللَّفْظِ وَحَرْفٌ وَاحِدٌ فِي الْكِتَابَةِ، كَمَدَّ، أَوْ حَرْفَانِ فِي اللَّفْظِ وَالْكِتَابَةِ، كَالرَّحْمَنِ.
text.en: When two letters of one kind come together, or two letters close in their point of articulation, the first is assimilated into the second because of the heaviness of what is repeated, as madda “he stretched”, and as akhraja shaṭʾahu “it sends forth its shoot” [48:29]. A group said: idghām is holding the letter in its point of articulation for as long as two letters are held; so it is reported from the great scholar Jār Allāh [al-Zamakhsharī]. And it is said: [it is] making the first unvowelled and folding it into the second. The letter assimilated is two letters in pronunciation and one letter in writing, as madda, or two letters in pronunciation and in writing, as al-raḥmāni “the Merciful”.

lessons.title: When both letters are vowelled, and when the first is quiescent
body: Two like letters can meet in three ways, and the whole chapter is built on them. The first: both are vowelled. Then idghām is necessary, as madda from madada. Two exceptions. Attached forms (ilḥāqiyyāt), as qardad, “rough high ground”, keep their letters apart “so that the attachment is not undone”: qardad is built to match a four-letter pattern, and merging would break the match. And some patterns stay apart to avoid confusion: ṣakak, surur, judad, ṭalal, which merged would sound like ṣakk, surr, judd, ṭall, quite other words.

Is there no confusion in the verb? Radda could come from radada or from raduda, farra from farara or farira, ʿaḍḍa from ʿaḍaḍa or ʿaḍiḍa. The future settles it, with one fact about the doubled verb: it never comes from three of the six bābs. Yaruddu could be faʿala or faʿula, but the doubled “does not come from faʿula yafʿulu”, so radda is radada. Yafirru could be faʿala or faʿila, but not faʿila yafʿilu, so farra is farara. Yaʿaḍḍu could be faʿala or faʿila, but not faʿala yafʿalu, so ʿaḍḍa is ʿaḍiḍa.

Ḥayiya, “he lived”, is not merged “in some dialects”, so that the ḍamma does not fall on the yāʾ in the future: a merged ḥayya would want a future like yaḥayyu, as a gloss in the print explains, and the language says yaḥyā. Others say the last yāʾ is not constant: it falls away in ḥayū and turns into alif in yaḥyā, so it cannot be relied on for idghām.
The second way: the first letter is quiescent. Then idghām is necessary “by necessity”, as madd, the maṣdar on faʿl: two like letters, the first without a vowel, can only be said as one long letter.
So far the rule is simple: when the second letter has a vowel, merge. The third way, where the second letter is quiescent, is the next lesson.

terms.en: attached forms, which keep their like letters apart
necessary assimilation: both vowelled, or the first quiescent
confusion of one form with another, which the rules avoid
the yāʾ that is not constant, as in ḥayiya

examples.en: qardad: an attached form, not merged
ṣakak, surur, judad, ṭalal: kept apart to avoid confusion
ḥayiya, yaḥyā: not merged in some dialects
madd: the first quiescent, merged by necessity

tasks.prompt: How do we know that radda is radada and not raduda?
tasks.answer: The future yaruddu fits faʿala yafʿulu or faʿula yafʿulu; but the doubled verb does not come from faʿula yafʿulu, so the base is radada.

tasks.prompt: Do the same for farra and ʿaḍḍa.
tasks.answer: Yafirru fits faʿala or faʿila with yafʿilu; the doubled does not come from faʿila yafʿilu, so farra is farara. Yaʿaḍḍu fits faʿala or faʿila with yafʿalu; the doubled does not come from faʿala yafʿalu, so ʿaḍḍa is ʿaḍiḍa.

tasks.prompt: Why is qardad not merged?
tasks.answer: It is an attached form, built to match a four-letter pattern; merging the two dāls would undo the attachment.

tasks.prompt: Give the two reasons why ḥayiya is left unmerged in some dialects.
tasks.answer: So that the ḍamma would not fall on the yāʾ in the future (a merged past would want yaḥayyu, while the language says yaḥyā); and because the last yāʾ is not constant: it drops in ḥayū and becomes alif in yaḥyā.

quiz.prompt: When both like letters are vowelled, idghām is…
quiz.explanation: As madda; except attached forms and confusing patterns.

quiz.prompt: Why is qardad not merged?
options: So that the attachment is not undone
quiz.explanation: It is an ilḥāqī form.

quiz.prompt: Surur is kept apart so that it is not taken for…
quiz.explanation: Surr, “navel-string”.

quiz.prompt: The doubled verb does not come from…
quiz.explanation: So radda is radada, not raduda.

quiz.prompt: ʿAḍḍa is ʿaḍiḍa, not ʿaḍaḍa, because…
options: the ḍād is a throat letter
the doubled does not come from faʿala yafʿalu
quiz.explanation: Yaʿaḍḍu then must be faʿila yafʿalu.

quiz.prompt: When the first like letter is quiescent, idghām is…
quiz.explanation: Madd: by necessity.

quiz.prompt: Why is ḥayiya not merged in some dialects?
options: So the ḍamma does not fall on the yāʾ in the future
quiz.explanation: The future is yaḥyā.

text.original: اجْتِمَاعُ الْحَرْفَيْنِ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَضْرُبٍ: الْأَوَّلُ أَنْ يَكُونَا مُتَحَرِّكَيْنِ، يَجِبُ فِيهِ الْإِدْغَامُ، إِلَّا فِي الْإِلْحَاقِيَّاتِ، نَحْوُ: قَرْدَدٍ، حَتَّى لَا يَبْطُلَ الْإِلْحَاقُ، وَالْأَوْزَانِ الَّتِي يَلْزَمُ الِالْتِبَاسُ، مِثْلُ: صَكَكٍ وَسُرُرٍ وَجُدَدٍ وَطَلَلٍ، حَتَّى لَا يَلْتَبِسَ بِصَكٍّ وَسُرٍّ وَجُدٍّ وَطَلٍّ.
text.en: The coming together of the two letters is of three kinds. The first: that both are vowelled. Idghām is necessary in it, except in the attached forms (ilḥāqiyyāt), as qardadin “rough high ground”, so that the attachment is not undone; and [except in] the patterns in which a confusion would follow, like ṣakakin “knocking of the knees”, sururin “couches”, judadin “streaks” and ṭalalin “traces of a dwelling”, so that they are not confused with ṣakkin “a written deed”, surrin “navel-string”, juddin “an old well” and ṭallin “dew”.

text.original: وَلَا يَلْتَبِسُ فِي مِثْلِ: رَدَّ وَفَرَّ وَعَضَّ؛ لِأَنَّ رَدَّ عُلِمَ مِنْ يَرُدُّ أَنَّ أَصْلَهُ رَدَدَ؛ لِأَنَّ الْمُضَاعَفَ لَا يَجِيءُ مِنْ فَعُلَ يَفْعُلُ، وَفَرَّ أَيْضًا يُعْلَمُ مِنْ يَفِرُّ؛ لِأَنَّ الْمُضَاعَفَ لَا يَجِيءُ مِنْ فَعِلَ يَفْعِلُ، وَعَضَّ أَيْضًا يُعْلَمُ مِنْ يَعَضُّ؛ لِأَنَّ الْمُضَاعَفَ لَا يَجِيءُ مِنْ فَعَلَ يَفْعَلُ.
text.en: There is no confusion in the like of radda “he returned”, farra “he fled” and ʿaḍḍa “he bit”: for of radda it is known from yaruddu that its origin is radada, because the doubled does not come from faʿula yafʿulu; and farra too is known from yafirru, because the doubled does not come from faʿila yafʿilu; and ʿaḍḍa too is known from yaʿaḍḍu, because the doubled does not come from faʿala yafʿalu.

text.original: وَلَا يُدْغَمُ حَيِيَ فِي بَعْضِ اللُّغَاتِ حَتَّى لَا يَقَعَ الضَّمَّةُ عَلَى الْيَاءِ فِي يَحْيَى، وَقِيلَ: الْيَاءُ الْأَخِيرَةُ غَيْرُ لَازِمَةٍ؛ لِأَنَّهُ تَسْقُطُ تَارَةً، نَحْوُ: حَيُوا، وَتُقْلَبُ تَارَةً، نَحْوُ: يَحْيَى. وَالثَّانِي أَنْ يَكُونَ الْأَوَّلُ سَاكِنًا، يَجِبُ فِيهِ الْإِدْغَامُ ضَرُورَةً، نَحْوُ: مَدٍّ عَلَى وَزْنِ فَعْلٍ.
text.en: ḥayiya “he lived” is not assimilated in some dialects, so that the ḍamma does not fall on the yāʾ in yaḥyā “he lives”; and it is said: [because] the last yāʾ is not constant, since it falls away at times, as ḥayū “they lived”, and is changed at times, as yaḥyā. The second: that the first is unvowelled. Idghām is necessary in it, by necessity, as maddin “stretching”, on the pattern faʿl.

lessons.title: When the second letter is quiescent: ẓaltu and qirna
body: The third way: the second like letter is quiescent. Then idghām is impossible, “because the condition of idghām is missing, which is that the second be vowelled”: you cannot fold a letter into one that has no vowel to carry it. A second reason: to merge, the first would have to be made quiescent too, “so two unvowelled letters come together, and one flees from one pitfall and falls into another”. A third: the word is already light, with its quiescent letter, so idghām has nothing to gain.
“But they allowed dropping in some places”, since two like letters still stand side by side: ẓaltu, “I remained”, said with one lām. They allowed changing a letter too, as in taqaḍḍā al-bāzī.

On dropping rests a reading of 33:33, wa-qirna fī buyūtikunna, “and stay in your houses”, if it is from al-qarār, “staying”. Its origin is iqrirna, a command to women in which the second rāʾ is quiescent before -na. The first rāʾ was dropped and its kasra moved to the qāf; the hamza of joining, no longer needed before a vowelled letter, was dropped too: qirna. Others take qirna from waqara yaqiru, “to be calm and dignified”, as the command of a mithāl (chapter four).

The other reading, wa-qarna, with a fatḥa, is the one of the Ḥafṣ copies of the Qurʾān most used today. The book derives it from qarra bi-l-makān, “he stayed in the place”, a dialect form with a fatḥa in the future (of the bāb of ʿalima, as a gloss in the print explains): origin iqrarna; the first rāʾ's fatḥa moved to the qāf, and the rest as before: qarna.

The lesson for the reader: when a doubled verb meets -tu, -na, -nā, the two letters stay apart (madadtu, umdudna); a form with one letter missing, like ẓaltu or qirna, is a permitted shortening, and the vowel left on the first letter is the trace of the letter that went.

moving a vowel to the letter before

tasks.prompt: Give the three reasons why idghām is impossible when the second letter is quiescent.
tasks.answer: Its condition, a vowel on the second letter, is missing; merging would mean making the first quiescent too, so two quiescent letters would meet (fleeing one pitfall into another); and the word is already light with its quiescent letter.

text.original: وَالثَّالِثُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الثَّانِي سَاكِنًا، فَالْإِدْغَامُ فِيهِ مُمْتَنِعٌ لِعَدَمِ شَرْطِ الْإِدْغَامِ، وَهُوَ تَحَرُّكُ الثَّانِي، وَقِيلَ: لَا بُدَّ مِنْ تَسْكِينِ الْأَوَّلِ، فَيَجْتَمِعُ سَاكِنَانِ، فَيَفِرُّ مِنْ وَرْطَةٍ وَيَقَعُ فِي أُخْرَى، وَقِيلَ: لِوُجُودِ الْخِفَّةِ بِالسَّاكِنِ مَعَ عَدَمِ شَرْطِ الْإِدْغَامِ.
text.en: The third: that the second is unvowelled. Then idghām in it is impossible, because the condition of idghām is missing, which is that the second be vowelled. And it is said: [because] the first must be made unvowelled, so two unvowelled letters come together, and one flees from one pitfall and falls into another. And it is said: because lightness is found with the unvowelled letter, together with the condition of idghām being missing.

text.original: وَلَكِنْ جَوَّزُوا الْحَذْفَ فِي بَعْضِ الْمَوَاضِعِ نَظَرًا إِلَى اجْتِمَاعِ الْمُتَجَانِسَيْنِ، نَحْوُ: ظَلْتُ، كَمَا جَوَّزُوا الْقَلْبَ فِي نَحْوِ: تَقَضَّى الْبَازِي، وَعَلَيْهِ قِرَاءَةُ مَنْ قَرَأَ: ﴿وَقِرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾ مِنَ الْقَرَارِ، أَصْلُهُ اقْرِرْنَ، فَحُذِفَتِ الرَّاءُ الْأُولَى، فَنُقِلَ حَرَكَتُهَا إِلَى الْقَافِ، ثُمَّ حُذِفَتِ الْهَمْزَةُ لِعَدَمِ الِاحْتِيَاجِ إِلَيْهَا، فَصَارَ قِرْنَ. وَقِيلَ: مِنْ وَقَرَ يَقِرُ وَقَارًا. وَإِذَا قُرِئَ: ﴿وَقَرْنَ﴾ بِفَتْحِ الْقَافِ يَكُونُ مِنْ قَرَّ بِالْمَكَانِ بِفَتْحِ الْقَافِ، وَهُوَ لُغَةٌ فِي قَرَّ، فَيَكُونُ أَصْلُهُ اقْرَرْنَ، فَنُقِلَ حَرَكَةُ الرَّاءِ إِلَى الْقَافِ، فَصَارَ قَرْنَ.
text.en: But they allowed dropping in some places, in view of the coming together of the two like letters, as ẓaltu “I remained”, as they allowed changing [a letter] in the like of taqaḍḍā al-bāzī “the falcon swooped down”. On this rests the reading of those who read wa-qirna fī buyūtikunna “and stay in your houses” [33:33], from al-qarāri “staying”: its origin is iqrirna; the first rāʾ was dropped and its vowel moved to the qāf, then the hamza was dropped because it was no longer needed, and it became qirna. And it is said: [it is] from waqara yaqiru waqāran “to be calm and dignified”. And when it is read wa-qarna, with a fatḥa on the qāf, it is from qarra bi-al-makāni “he stayed in the place”, with a fatḥa on the qāf, which is a dialect form of qarra; so its origin is iqrarna, the vowel of the rāʾ was moved to the qāf, and it became qarna.

lessons.title: The accidental sukūn, and the full conjugation of madda
body: The last rule held “when its sukūn is constant”, as before -na and -tu, which always make the letter before them quiescent. “When it is accidental, idghām and its absence are both allowed.” The accidental sukūn is the one of the jussive and the command: umdud, “stretch!”, may stay apart, or merge.

If merged, the second dāl needs a vowel, and three are allowed: mudda, “with a fatḥa for lightness”; muddi, “with the kasra, because the kasra is the original in giving a vowel to an unvowelled letter”; and muddu, “with the ḍamma, for harmony” with the ḍamma of the mīm. That is why firru is not allowed: farra has a kasra in the future, firra and firri only, with no ḍamma to harmonise with.
But umdudna, “stretch! (women)”, is never merged, “because the sukūn of the second is constant”: the -na of the women always has a quiescent letter before it.

The book then gives the rest. With the heavy nūn: muddanna, muddānni, muddunna, muddinna, muddānni, umdudnānni; with the light: muddan, muddun, muddin. The doer māddun, the one done to mamdūdun, the noun of time and place mamaddun, the instrument mimaddun, and the passive mudda yumaddu. Each is made as from the sound verb and then merged wherever the second dāl has a vowel.

Notice in the nūn forms that the women's form alone is unmerged, umdudnānni: the nūn of the women keeps its quiescent letter even when the nūn of emphasis follows. The conjugation tool does not conjugate doubled verbs; these forms are the print's.

accidental sukūn: of the jussive and command; idghām allowed

the kasra is the original vowel for moving a quiescent letter

mudda, muddi, muddu: the merged command with each vowel

tasks.answer: The sukūn of the second dāl in umdud is accidental (that of the command), so idghām is allowed and so is its absence. In umdudna the sukūn before -na is constant, so idghām is impossible.

tasks.prompt: Explain the three vowels of the merged command: mudda, muddi, muddu.
tasks.answer: Mudda with fatḥa for lightness; muddi with kasra, the original vowel for moving a quiescent letter; muddu with ḍamma, in harmony with the ḍamma of the mīm.

tasks.prompt: Why is firru not allowed?
tasks.answer: The ḍamma is allowed only for harmony with a ḍamma before it; farra yafirru has a kasra, so the command is firra or firri, never firru.

tasks.prompt: List the derived forms of madda that the book gives.
tasks.answer: The doer māddun, the one done to mamdūdun, the noun of time and place mamaddun, the instrument mimaddun, and the passive mudda yumaddu.

text.original: هَذَا إِذَا كَانَ سُكُونُهُ لَازِمًا، وَإِذَا كَانَ عَارِضًا يَجُوزُ الْإِدْغَامُ وَعَدَمُهُ، نَحْوُ: امْدُدْ، وَمُدَّ بِفَتْحِ الدَّالِ لِلْخِفَّةِ، وَمُدِّ بِالْكَسْرِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْكَسْرَ أَصْلٌ فِي تَحْرِيكِ السَّاكِنِ، وَمُدُّ بِالضَّمِّ لِلْإِتْبَاعِ، وَمِنْ ثَمَّةَ لَا يَجُوزُ فِرُّ لِعَدَمِ الْإِتْبَاعِ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ الْإِدْغَامُ فِي امْدُدْنَ؛ لِأَنَّ سُكُونَ الثَّانِي لَازِمٌ.
text.en: This is when its sukūn is constant. When it is accidental, idghām and its absence are both allowed, as umdud “stretch!”, and mudda with a fatḥa on the dāl, for lightness, and muddi with the kasra, because the kasra is the original in giving a vowel to an unvowelled letter, and muddu with the ḍamma, for harmony [with the ḍamma before it]. For that reason firru is not allowed, since there is no harmony. Idghām is not allowed in umdudna “stretch! (f. pl.)”, because the sukūn of the second is constant.

text.original: وَتَقُولُ بِالنُّونِ الثَّقِيلَةِ: مُدَّنَّ مُدَّانِّ مُدُّنَّ مُدِّنَّ مُدَّانِّ امْدُدْنَانِّ، وَبِالْخَفِيفَةِ: مُدَّنْ مُدُّنْ مُدِّنْ. الْفَاعِلُ: مَادٌّ، وَالْمَفْعُولُ: مَمْدُودٌ، وَاسْمُ الزَّمَانِ وَالْمَكَانِ: مَمَدٌّ، وَاسْمُ الْآلَةِ: مِمَدٌّ، وَالْمَجْهُولُ: مُدَّ يُمَدُّ.
text.en: With the heavy nūn you say: muddanna muddānni muddunna muddinna muddānni umdudnānni “do stretch!” (to one man, two, men; to one woman, two, women), and with the light: muddan muddun muddin. The fāʿil is māddun “stretching”, the mafʿūl mamdūdun “stretched”, the noun of time and place mamaddun, the noun of instrument mimaddun, and the passive mudda yumaddu “to be stretched”.

lessons.title: The tāʾ of iftiʿāl after thāʾ, dāl, dhāl, zāy, sīn and shīn
body: Idghām also works between unlike letters, above all in iftaʿala, where the added tāʾ stands right after the first root letter. When that letter is one of twelve, hamza, tāʾ, thāʾ, dāl, dhāl, zāy, sīn, shīn, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ or ẓāʾ, the tāʾ may be merged with it. (The first word of the rule is cramped in the print; it may read “is necessary” rather than “is allowed”.) Ittakhadha, “he took”, from a hamza root, is merged irregularly; ittajara, “he traded”, merges two tāʾs; ittaʾara, from th-ʾ-r, “to take revenge”, may also be said iththaʾara.

Why both ways in ittaʾara? Because the tāʾ and the thāʾ are both “whispered” (mahmūsa) letters, said without voice, gathered in the phrase satashḥathuka Khaṣafah. Being one in that quality, they count as of one kind, and either can become the other.

Iddāna, “he borrowed”, from d-y-n, admits only one form. The tāʾ is made a dāl, being far from it in voice (the dāl is voiced) and near it in point of articulation; then two dāls meet and must merge. Idhdhakara, “he remembered”, goes further: the tāʾ becomes a dāl as in iddāna; then, the dāl and the dhāl both being voiced (majhūra), one may merge either way, iddakara (as in the Qurʾān's fa-hal min muddakirin, 54:15) or idhdhakara, or keep them apart, since they are not one letter “in essence”.

Izzāna, “he adorned himself”, is like idhdhakara, but the zāy may not be turned into a dāl: “the zāy is greater than the dāl in the drawing out of the sound”, and turning it into a dāl would be “like putting a large bowl into a small one”. Issamaʿa, “he listened”, may merge, the sīn and the tāʾ both being whispered, but only by turning the tāʾ into a sīn, never the sīn into a tāʾ, for the same reason; and keeping them apart is allowed: that is the everyday istamaʿa. Ishshabaha, beside ishtabaha, is the same.
One principle runs through these cases: the added tāʾ gives way, and a letter with a fuller sound (the hissing zāy, sīn, shīn) is never turned into a lesser one.

terms.en: the added tāʾ of the pattern iftaʿala
the whispered (voiceless) letters: satashḥathuka Khaṣafah
the voiced letters, as dāl and dhāl
keeping the two letters apart, unmerged
the drawing out of the sound, in which zāy and sīn are “greater”

examples.en: ittakhadha: merged irregularly
ittaʾara, iththaʾara: the whispered tāʾ and thāʾ, either way
iddakara, idhdhakara: merged either way
istamaʿa, ishtabaha: the letters kept apart (conjugation tool)

tasks.prompt: Why can ittaʾara also be said iththaʾara?
tasks.answer: The tāʾ and the thāʾ are both whispered letters, so they count as of one kind; one may merge by turning the tāʾ into a thāʾ or the thāʾ into a tāʾ.

tasks.prompt: Explain iddāna step by step.
tasks.answer: From d-y-n on iftaʿala. The tāʾ is far from the dāl in voice and near it in articulation, so it is turned into a dāl; then two dāls of one kind meet and must be merged: iddāna. No other form is allowed.

tasks.prompt: Why may one say issamaʿa but never turn the sīn into a tāʾ?
tasks.answer: Both are whispered, so merging is allowed by turning the tāʾ into a sīn. The sīn is greater in the drawing out of the sound, and a greater letter is not turned into a lesser; keeping them apart, istamaʿa, is also allowed.

tasks.prompt: Give the forms allowed from dh-k-r on iftaʿala.
tasks.answer: The tāʾ becomes a dāl; then iddakara (dhāl made dāl), idhdhakara (dāl made dhāl), or the two kept apart, since they are both voiced but not one letter in essence.

text.original: وَيَجُوزُ الْإِدْغَامُ إِذَا وَقَعَ قَبْلَ تَاءِ الِافْتِعَالِ حَرْفٌ مِنْ حُرُوفِ «اَتَثَدَذَزَسَشَصَضَطَظَ»، نَحْوُ: اتَّخَذَ، شَاذٌّ، وَنَحْوُ: اتَّجَرَ وَاتَّأَرَ، وَيَجُوزُ فِيهِ اثَّأَرَ؛ لِأَنَّ التَّاءَ وَالثَّاءَ مِنَ الْمَهْمُوسَةِ، وَحُرُوفُهَا: «سَتَشْحَثُكَ خَصَفَهْ»، فَيَكُونَانِ مِنْ جِنْسٍ وَاحِدٍ نَظَرًا إِلَى الْمَهْمُوسَةِ، فَيَجُوزُ لَكَ الْإِدْغَامُ بِجَعْلِ التَّاءِ ثَاءً، وَالثَّاءِ تَاءً.
text.en: Idghām is allowed when, before the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, there stands one of the letters alif [that is, hamza], tāʾ, thāʾ, dāl, dhāl, zāy, sīn, shīn, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ, as ittakhadha “he took”, which is irregular, and as ittajara “he traded” and ittaʾara “he took revenge”. In the last iththaʾara is also allowed, because the tāʾ and the thāʾ are among the whispered letters (mahmūsa), whose letters are [gathered in] satashḥathuka Khaṣafah “Khaṣafa will beg of you”; so the two are of one kind in view of the whispering, and you may assimilate by making the tāʾ a thāʾ, or the thāʾ a tāʾ.

text.original: وَنَحْوُ: ادَّانَ لَا يَجُوزُ فِيهِ غَيْرُ إِدْغَامِ الدَّالِ فِي الدَّالِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ إِذَا جُعِلَتِ التَّاءُ دَالًا لِبُعْدِهِ مِنَ الدَّالِ فِي الْمَهْمُوسَةِ، وَلِقُرْبِ الدَّالِ مِنَ التَّاءِ فِي الْمَخْرَجِ، يَلْزَمُ حِينَئِذٍ حَرْفَانِ مِنْ جِنْسٍ وَاحِدٍ، فَيُدْغَمُ.
text.en: The like of iddāna “he borrowed” admits nothing but the assimilation of the dāl into the dāl: for when the tāʾ is made a dāl — because of its distance from the dāl in the whispering, and because the dāl is close to the tāʾ in the point of articulation — two letters of one kind then come together, and it is assimilated.

text.original: وَنَحْوُ: اذَّكَرَ يَجُوزُ فِيهِ ادَّكَرَ وَاذَّكَرَ؛ لِأَنَّ الدَّالَ وَالذَّالَ مِنَ الْمَجْهُورَةِ، فَجُعِلَ التَّاءُ دَالًا كَمَا فِي ادَّانَ، فَيَجُوزُ لَكَ الْإِدْغَامُ نَظَرًا إِلَى اتِّحَادِهِمَا فِي الْمَجْهُورَةِ بِجَعْلِ الذَّالِ دَالًا، أَوِ الدَّالِ ذَالًا، وَالْبَيَانُ نَظَرًا إِلَى عَدَمِ اتِّحَادِهِمَا فِي الذَّاتِ.
text.en: The like of idhdhakara “he remembered” admits iddakara and idhdhakara: because the dāl and the dhāl are among the voiced letters (majhūra), the tāʾ was made a dāl, as in iddāna; then you may assimilate, in view of their being one in the voicing, by making the dhāl a dāl or the dāl a dhāl; and [you may] keep them apart (bayān), in view of their not being one in essence.

text.original: وَنَحْوُ: ازَّانَ مِثْلُ اذَّكَرَ، وَلَكِنْ لَا يَجُوزُ فِيهِ الْإِدْغَامُ بِجَعْلِ الزَّاءِ دَالًا؛ لِأَنَّ الزَّاءَ أَعْظَمُ مِنَ الدَّالِ فِي امْتِدَادِ الصَّوْتِ، فَيَصِيرُ حِينَئِذٍ كَوَضْعِ الْقَصْعَةِ الْكَبِيرَةِ فِي الصَّغِيرَةِ، أَوْ لِأَنَّهُ يُوَازِي بِادَّانَ. وَنَحْوُ: اسَّمَعَ يَجُوزُ فِيهِ الْإِدْغَامُ؛ لِأَنَّ السِّينَ وَالتَّاءَ مِنَ الْمَهْمُوسَةِ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ الْإِدْغَامُ بِجَعْلِ السِّينِ تَاءً لِعِظَمِ السِّينِ فِي امْتِدَادِ الصَّوْتِ، وَيَجُوزُ الْبَيَانُ لِعَدَمِ الْجِنْسِيَّةِ فِي الذَّاتِ، وَنَحْوُ: اشَّبَهَ مِثْلُ اسَّمَعَ.
text.en: The like of izzāna “he adorned himself” is like idhdhakara; but idghām is not allowed in it by making the zāy a dāl, because the zāy is greater than the dāl in the drawing out of the sound, and it would then be like putting a large bowl into a small one; or because it would be on a par with iddāna. The like of issamaʿa “he listened” admits idghām, because the sīn and the tāʾ are among the whispered letters; but idghām by making the sīn a tāʾ is not allowed, because of the greatness of the sīn in the drawing out of the sound; and keeping them apart is allowed, since they are not of one kind in essence. The like of ishshabaha “it was doubtful” is like issamaʿa.

lessons.title: The tāʾ of iftiʿāl after ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ and ẓāʾ
body: With the four heavy letters the tāʾ first changes, then may merge. Iṣṣabara, “he was patient”, admits iṣṭabara “because the ṣād is among the raised and covered letters”: ṣād, ṭāʾ, ḍād and ẓāʾ are raised and covered (mustaʿliya muṭbaqa), said with the back of the tongue lifted and the tongue spread under the palate; khāʾ, ghayn and qāf are raised only. The tāʾ is a “lowered” letter. So the tāʾ is changed into a ṭāʾ, its heavy twin: far from the ṣād in quality, but near it in point of articulation. That gives iṣṭabara.
The book compares sitt, “six”, from sids: there the sīn and the dāl were both turned into tāʾ, the sīn being near the tāʾ in whispering and the tāʾ near the dāl in articulation, and then merged.

Then, from iṣṭabara, “you may assimilate by making the ṭāʾ a ṣād”, both being raised: iṣṣabara. But not the ṣād a ṭāʾ, “because of the greatness of the ṣād”: one never says iṭṭabara. Keeping them apart, iṣṭabara, is allowed. Iḍḍaraba is the same: iḍḍaraba and iḍṭaraba are allowed, “and iṭṭaraba is not allowed, because of the added quality of the ḍād”.

Iṭṭalaba, “he sought”, admits only idghām: the tāʾ turns into a ṭāʾ, and two ṭāʾs meet. Iẓẓalama, “he bore a wrong”, may merge either way, the ṭāʾ to ẓāʾ or the ẓāʾ to ṭāʾ, “because the two are equal in greatness”, or stay apart: iẓẓalama, iṭṭalama, iẓṭalama.

In everyday Arabic you meet the forms with ṭāʾ: iṣṭabara, iḍṭaraba, iṭṭalaba, which the conjugation tool gives. The change of tāʾ into ṭāʾ in iftaʿala after these letters is necessary, as the list of substitutions says later (lesson 60); the merging that may follow is a choice.

terms.en: the raised letters: ṣ, ṭ, ḍ, ẓ, kh, gh, q
the covered letters: ṣ, ṭ, ḍ, ẓ
the lowered letters, as the tāʾ
changing one letter into another, as tāʾ into ṭāʾ

examples.en: iṣṣabara, iṣṭabara: merged, or with the tāʾ made ṭāʾ
sitt, from sids: sīn and dāl made tāʾ and merged
iṭṭabara: never said
iẓẓalama, iṭṭalama, iẓṭalama: all three allowed

tasks.prompt: Derive iṣṭabara from ṣ-b-r on iftaʿala, and then iṣṣabara.
tasks.answer: The ṣād is raised and covered, the tāʾ lowered; being far in quality and near in articulation, the tāʾ is changed into a ṭāʾ: iṣṭabara. Then, ṣād and ṭāʾ both being raised, one may merge by turning the ṭāʾ into a ṣād: iṣṣabara.

tasks.prompt: Why is iṭṭabara not said, while iṭṭalama is?
tasks.answer: The ṣād is greater than the ṭāʾ, and a greater letter is not turned into a lesser, so the ṣād cannot become a ṭāʾ. The ẓāʾ and the ṭāʾ are equal in greatness, so either may become the other.

tasks.prompt: Why does iṭṭalaba admit only the merged form?
tasks.answer: The tāʾ of iftiʿāl becomes a ṭāʾ, near it in articulation, and then two ṭāʾs, letters of one kind, meet; idghām of like letters, both vowelled, is necessary.

quiz.prompt: Which are the raised and covered letters?
quiz.explanation: Khāʾ, ghayn and qāf are raised only.

quiz.prompt: In iṣṭabara the tāʾ became a ṭāʾ because…
options: it is far from the ṣād in quality and near the ṭāʾ in articulation
quiz.explanation: The heavy twin of the tāʾ suits the ṣād.

quiz.prompt: Which form is never said?
quiz.explanation: The ṣād is not made a ṭāʾ.

quiz.prompt: Iṭṭaraba is not allowed because of…
options: the added quality of the ḍād
quiz.explanation: Iḍḍaraba and iḍṭaraba are allowed.

quiz.prompt: Iṭṭalaba admits…
quiz.explanation: Two ṭāʾs meet.

quiz.prompt: Why may iẓẓalama merge either way?
options: The ẓāʾ and the ṭāʾ are equal in greatness
quiz.explanation: Iẓẓalama, iṭṭalama, iẓṭalama.

quiz.prompt: Sitt, “six”, comes from…
quiz.explanation: Sīn and dāl made tāʾ, then merged.

text.original: وَنَحْوُ: اصَّبَرَ يَجُوزُ فِيهِ اصْطَبَرَ؛ لِأَنَّ الصَّادَ مِنَ الْمُسْتَعْلِيَةِ الْمُطْبَقَةِ، وَحُرُوفُهَا: «صَطَضَظَ خَغَقَ»، الْأَرْبَعَةُ الْأُولَى مُسْتَعْلِيَةٌ مُطْبَقَةٌ، وَالثَّلَاثَةُ الْأَخِيرَةُ مُسْتَعْلِيَةٌ فَقَطْ، وَالتَّاءُ مِنَ الْمُنْخَفِضَةِ، فَجُعِلَ التَّاءُ طَاءً لِمُبَاعَدَةٍ بَيْنَهُمَا، وَقُرْبِ التَّاءِ مِنَ الطَّاءِ فِي الْمَخْرَجِ، فَصَارَ اصْطَبَرَ، كَمَا فِي سِتٍّ، أَصْلُهُ سِدْسٌ، فَجُعِلَ السِّينُ وَالدَّالُ تَاءً لِقُرْبِ السِّينِ مِنَ التَّاءِ فِي الْمَهْمُوسَةِ، وَالتَّاءِ مِنَ الدَّالِ فِي الْمَخْرَجِ، ثُمَّ أُدْغِمَ.
text.en: The like of iṣṣabara “he was patient” admits iṣṭabara, because the ṣād is among the raised and covered letters (mustaʿliya muṭbaqa), whose letters are ṣād, ṭāʾ, ḍād, ẓāʾ, khāʾ, ghayn and qāf — the first four raised and covered, the last three raised only — while the tāʾ is among the lowered letters (munkhafiḍa); so the tāʾ was made a ṭāʾ, because of the distance between them and the nearness of the tāʾ to the ṭāʾ in the point of articulation, and it became iṣṭabara; as in sittin “six”, whose origin is sidsun: the sīn and the dāl were made a tāʾ, because the sīn is near the tāʾ in the whispering and the tāʾ near the dāl in the point of articulation; then it was assimilated.

text.original: ثُمَّ يَجُوزُ لَكَ الْإِدْغَامُ بِجَعْلِ الطَّاءِ صَادًا نَظَرًا إِلَى اتِّحَادِهِمَا فِي الِاسْتِعْلَائِيَّةِ، نَحْوُ: اصَّبَرَ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ لَكَ الْإِدْغَامُ بِجَعْلِ الصَّادِ طَاءً لِعِظَمِ الصَّادِ، أَعْنِي: لَا يُقَالُ: اطَّبَرَ، وَيَجُوزُ الْبَيَانُ لِعَدَمِ الْجِنْسِيَّةِ فِي الذَّاتِ. وَنَحْوُ: اضَّرَبَ مِثْلُ اصَّبَرَ، أَعْنِي: يَجُوزُ اضَّرَبَ وَاضْطَرَبَ، وَلَا يَجُوزُ اطَّرَبَ؛ لِزِيَادَةِ صِفَةِ الضَّادِ.
text.en: Then you may assimilate by making the ṭāʾ a ṣād, in view of their being one in the raising, as iṣṣabara; but you may not assimilate by making the ṣād a ṭāʾ, because of the greatness of the ṣād; I mean, one does not say iṭṭabara. Keeping them apart is allowed, since they are not of one kind in essence. The like of iḍḍaraba “it was agitated” is like iṣṣabara; I mean, iḍḍaraba and iḍṭaraba are allowed, and iṭṭaraba is not allowed, because of the added quality of the ḍād.

text.original: وَنَحْوُ: اطَّلَبَ لَا يَجُوزُ فِيهِ غَيْرُ الْإِدْغَامِ؛ لِاجْتِمَاعِ الْحَرْفَيْنِ مِنْ جِنْسٍ وَاحِدٍ بَعْدَ قَلْبِ تَاءِ الِافْتِعَالِ طَاءً لِقُرْبِ التَّاءِ مِنَ الطَّاءِ فِي الْمَخْرَجِ. وَنَحْوُ: اظَّلَمَ يَجُوزُ فِيهِ الْإِدْغَامُ بِجَعْلِ الطَّاءِ ظَاءً وَالظَّاءِ طَاءً؛ لِمُسَاوَاةٍ بَيْنَهُمَا فِي الْعِظَمِ، وَيَجُوزُ الْبَيَانُ لِعَدَمِ الْجِنْسِيَّةِ فِي الذَّاتِ، مِثْلُ: اظَّلَمَ وَاطَّلَمَ وَاظْطَلَمَ.
text.en: The like of iṭṭalaba “he sought” admits nothing but idghām, because two letters of one kind come together once the tāʾ of iftiʿāl has been changed into a ṭāʾ, because of the nearness of the tāʾ to the ṭāʾ in the point of articulation. The like of iẓẓalama “he bore a wrong” admits idghām by making the ṭāʾ a ẓāʾ and the ẓāʾ a ṭāʾ, because the two are equal in greatness; and keeping them apart is allowed, since they are not of one kind in essence: as iẓẓalama, iṭṭalama and iẓṭalama.

lessons.title: Ittaʿada and ittasara; the tāʾ merged into the ʿayn
lessons.arabic: اتَّعَدَ وَاتَّسَرَ، وَإِدْغَامُ التَّاءِ فِي الْعَيْنِ
lessons.transliteration: ittaʿada wa-ittasara, wa-idghām al-tāʾ fī al-ʿayn
body: When the first root letter is a wāw or a yāʾ, iftaʿala turns it into a tāʾ. Ittaʿada, “he accepted a promise”, from w-ʿ-d: had the wāw stayed, it would have become a yāʾ after the kasra of the hamza in the past, ītaʿada, and stayed a wāw in the future, yawtaʿidu: “the verb would be at one time with yāʾ and at another with wāw”. Turning it into a tāʾ, merged with the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, keeps one shape throughout. Ittasara, “he played at maysir”, from y-s-r: the yāʾ became a tāʾ, “fleeing from a succession of kasras”.

Ītakala, “he ate”, is not merged, though its yāʾ stands where the wāw of ittaʿada stood. That yāʾ “is not constant”: it is only the hamza of a-k-l softened after a kasra, and it “becomes a hamza when you make it triliteral”, akala. A letter that may turn back into something else is not a firm base for idghām, which is also why ḥayiya is left unmerged in some dialects; and ittakhadha, from the hamza root a-kh-dh, is merged only irregularly.

Now the tāʾ meets the letter after it. When the ʿayn is tāʾ, dāl, dhāl, zāy, sīn, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ or ẓāʾ, idghām is allowed: yaqattilu for yaqtatilu, yabaddilu, yaʿadhdhiru, yanazziʿu, yabassimu, yakhaṣṣimu, yafaḍḍilu, yalaṭṭimu, yanaẓẓiru. The vowel of the tāʾ moves back to the fāʾ, and the tāʾ becomes the ʿayn.

Only one direction is allowed here: “nothing is allowed except the idghām made by making the tāʾ like the ʿayn, because drawing the later letter to the earlier is weak”. In the last two lessons the tāʾ followed the letter before it; here it is pulled forward into the letter after it.

These merged futures are uncommon in prose, and the print leaves most of them unvowelled; we vowel them by the rule. The plain forms, yaqtatilu, yakhtaṣimu, yabtasimu, are what the conjugation tool gives and what you will usually read.

terms.en: turning a wāw or yāʾ into a tāʾ, as in ittaʿada
not constant: a letter that may turn back into another
merging the tāʾ of iftiʿāl into the ʿayn after it
drawing the later letter to the earlier: weak, so not done here

examples.en: ītaʿada, yawtaʿidu: the unstable shapes that ittaʿada avoids
ītakala: not merged, its yāʾ not constant
yaqattilu, yakhaṣṣimu, yabassimu: the tāʾ merged into the ʿayn
yaqtatilu, yakhtaṣimu, yabtasimu: the plain forms (conjugation tool)
